Adabor house takeover attempt foiled; 10 arrested
item.description:
Ten people have been arrested in a case filed over an alleged attempt to seize a house, vandalise property and extort money in Adabor, Dhaka, police said.
Four of the suspects, including two who were injured in police gunfire, were arrested during an overnight operation. Police said they opened fire in self-defence after the suspects allegedly attempted to attack officers with machetes.
The incident took place around 2:30am on Monday in an open area beside a canal behind a playground near Kacha Bazar in Naboday Housing, Adabor.
The two injured suspects were identified as Rajib Howlader, 30, and Sagar, 24. Both sustained gunshot wounds to their legs and were taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for treatment.
The other two arrested during the operation were identified as Shakib, 23, and Rashed, 24.
Adabor police said they launched the operation around 2am based on information about the suspects’ whereabouts. Seven to eight people were present at the scene.
When police attempted to arrest them, the suspects allegedly tried to attack officers with machetes. Police then fired two rounds from a shotgun carried by a constable in self-defence, according to police.
Rajib and Sagar were injured, while the others fled. Police recovered numerous weapons from the scene.
Adabor police station Officer-in-Charge Zahidul Islam said police opened fire after the suspects allegedly attempted to attack them.
“The injured were sent to hospital. Legal action will be taken in connection with the incident,” he said.
The OC said six people had previously been arrested in the case, and the four arrests during the overnight operation brought the total number of suspects arrested to 10.
According to police, Sagar has eight cases filed against him with Adabor and Mohammadpur police stations. Rajib is a named accused in the Babu murder case in Mohammadpur.
Shakib and Rashed each have five cases against them, police said.
On Sunday, a group of 15-20 people allegedly attacked a house in Shyamoli Housing, Adabor, carrying machetes, ramdas and pistols, in an alleged attempt to seize the property.
A case was filed with Adabor police station over the incident.
Police said the two sides had been involved in a longstanding dispute over ownership of the house and that a court case concerning the property is ongoing.

item.title: Gold prices drop further
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has reduced gold prices again, with the price of 22-carat hallmarked gold falling by Tk190 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat gold jewellery will cost Tk19,595 per gram.
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Tuesday.
The Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring set the new rates at a meeting at 9am on Tuesday. The decision was announced in a notification signed by the committee’s chairman, Dr Dewan Aminul Islam Shahin.
Under the new rates, 21-carat gold will cost Tk18,715 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,070. Gold sold under the traditional method has been priced at Tk13,130 per gram.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk2,28,477. Making charges will be added separately based on the design of the jewellery.
On Monday, September 28, Bajus had set the price of 22-carat gold at Tk19,785 per gram. The latest reduction brings the price down by Tk190 per gram in a single day.
The price had previously been reduced on September 26, when 22-carat gold was priced at Tk19,970 per gram.
Compared with September 26, the price of 22-carat gold has therefore fallen by Tk375 per gram, or approximately Tk4,374 per bhori , in three days.
Bajus has also reduced silver prices.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver will cost Tk370 per gram, 21-carat silver Tk355, 18-carat silver Tk305 and traditional-method silver Tk230 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk385 per gram on September 28, meaning it had fallen by Tk15 per gram in one day.
On September 26, 22-carat silver was priced at Tk415 per gram, representing a decline of Tk45 per gram over three days.
Bajus said making charges will apply separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
However, as VAT is already included in the fixed selling price, it cannot be charged separately to customers.
For exchanges involving old gold jewellery, 12% will be deducted, excluding making charges and the cost of stones. For purchases of old jewellery, the deduction will be 18%.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either exchange or purchase transactions, according to Bajus.
The new rates will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
Bajus said the new gold and silver prices were set after considering the overall market situation and a decline in the prices of raw gold and silver.

item.title: Bangladesh Missions abroad go offline due to technical issues with DIP server
item.description:
The government is working to address the technical issues as soon as possible and help the Bangladesh Missions abroad deal with visa processing issues, as the server is currently unavailable.
“Efforts are underway to address the technical issues as soon as possible,” a senior official told UNB on Monday night, noting that due to technical issues with the central system of the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, the MRV (Machine Readable Visa) server is currently unavailable.
He said all the Missions abroad are facing the same problem. A visa applicant who applied from a European country told UNB that he submitted his visa application online but has been unable to proceed with the process due to the technical issue.
“Although the system indicated that I would receive an email within 24 hours of submitting the application, I have not received any email so far, while repeated calls have gone unanswered,” said the applicant.
Due to the technical issues, the processing of NVR (No Visa Required (NVR)) and visa applications and the issuance of visas at the Bangladesh Missions abroad are experiencing a temporary delay.
The Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, is working to resolve the technical issues and restore the central system at the earliest possible time.
The government has requested the applicants to allow additional time for the processing of their applications and to refrain from making repeated enquiries regarding the status of their applications during this period.
Meanwhile, the Embassy of Bangladesh, Berlin, in an urgent notice, regretted any inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience, understanding and cooperation of all concerned.
Applicants will be informed via the websites and Facebook pages of the Missions abroad once the central system is restored and normal visa services resume.
Another official said the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) conveyed to the Missions abroad the information regarding the technical issues last week, as it is applicable to all.
The Embassy of Bangladesh in Bangkok, in a public message on Tuesday, said it informed all visa service seekers that, due to a temporary technical issue with the visa server, applicants may experience difficulties in submitting visa applications and/or receiving visa-related services.
The embassy said the concerned technical team is working to resolve the issue as soon as possible.
Applicants have been requested to bear with the temporary inconvenience and, where possible, avoid making urgent travel arrangements dependent on immediate visa processing until the system is fully restored.
The embassy regretted the inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience and understanding of all concerned.

item.title: DB arrests Jamaat MP’s son-in-law over attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio
item.description:
Detective Branch (DB) of police has arrested Mizanur Rahman, 59, the son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami’s Kushtia-2 constituency MP Md Abdul Gafur, in a case filed over an attack on New Guinea Properties in Dhaka’s ECB Chattar area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) DB chief and Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune on Tuesday morning.
He said investigators had obtained significant information by questioning those already arrested and that operations were underway to arrest others who may have been involved.
According to the DB chief, Major General (retd) Golam Mahiuuddin Chowdhury and Nazim Uddin, the owner of New Guinea Properties, have been involved in a longstanding dispute over the possession and control of 35 kathas of land.
He said people allegedly acting on behalf of Major General (retd) Golam Mahiuuddin Chowdhury entered the New Guinea Properties premises and vandalised several structures.
The DB chief said an investigation into Mahiuuddin Chowdhury’s alleged involvement was underway and that he would be questioned if necessary. Legal action would be taken if evidence of his involvement is found, he added.
On Monday around 5pm, a DB Gulshan Division team detained Mizanur Rahman from his residence in Dhaka’s West Matikata area, according to AFM Anwar Hossain, deputy commissioner of the DB’s Gulshan Division.
The DB said Mizanur was named accused No 9 in a case filed with Cantonment police station on September 27.
On Saturday night, unidentified individuals attacked New Guinea Properties in the ECB Chattar area.
During the attack, the Brownfish studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir was extensively vandalised and looted. Muqtadir had rented a floor of the New Guinea Properties-owned building and set up his studio there.
Police said the studio was also vandalised during the attack.

item.title: Shama highlights Bangladesh-US education cooperation in California
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam highlighted opportunities to deepen Bangladesh-US cooperation in education, science, research and technology during talks with Arizona State University (ASU) representatives in California.
A Bangladesh delegation led by Prime Minister’s Adviser for Finance and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir met the ASU representatives at the Four Seasons Hotel Silicon Valley on September 27, said a foreign ministry’s press release Tuesday morning.
The talks focused on linking engineering education, research, workforce development, industry and investment to build a semiconductor ecosystem in Bangladesh.
Potential areas of cooperation included microelectronics curricula, faculty training, applied research and partnerships between universities and industry.
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Boby Hajjaj underscored STEM education and teacher development, while Prime Minister’s Adviser Rehan Asif Asad called for a semiconductor roadmap connecting research and education with investment and commercial use.
Titumir stressed sustainable planning and stronger links between education and industry to turn technology partnerships into skilled jobs, research capacity and investment.
The two sides also explored cooperation with ASU’s University Design Institute on higher education reform.
They discussed developing a memorandum of understanding covering semiconductor education, workforce and faculty development, research and institutional cooperation.
Prime Minister’s Protocol Officer-2 Kamrul Islam, Deputy Press Secretary-1 Md Jahidul Islam, Bangladesh ambassador to the US Tareq Md Ariful Islam, and Consul General in Los Angeles Kazi Muhammad Jabed Iqbal also participated.
Bangladesh’s Consulate General in Los Angeles will facilitate follow-up discussions to identify specific projects and partner institutions, the release said.

item.title: Beyond the bottom line
item.description:
The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) opened its January spectrum auction, expecting the high-stakes competition typical of vital national infrastructure sales. Instead, the room fell silent.
Grameenphone acquired 10 MHz of the 700 MHz band at the base reserve price of Tk 2,370 crore, Robi withdrew, while Banglalink stayed away from the bidding, leaving 10 MHz of the unsold spectrum to be assigned later to state-owned Teletalk at the same rate.
Failing to attract competition, this transaction left policy-makers with a critical question: How can such an auction dictate the pricing of an upcoming renewal cycle?
The short answer is it cannot . True market value requires viable alternatives where operators bid for expansion, not survival. Spectrum renewal offers no such luxury.
Once a mobile operator anchors its network architecture around a specific band and deploys thousands of base stations, walking away is no longer an option. A renewal price has little to do with market value; it is apparently a reflection of short-term state treasury demands colliding with an operator's inability to walk away without shutting down their business.
This structural disconnect matters as Bangladesh approaches the November renewal of spectrum in the 900 MHz, 1.8 GHz, and 2.1 GHz bands. Data from the GSMA’s 2025 study reveals that Bangladesh’s spectrum costs consume 15.7% of operators’ recurring revenues, much higher than the Asia-Pacific median of 10.4% and the global median of 7.7%.
Macroeconomic modeling suggests that cutting this economic burden to half could unlock $34 billion in cumulative economic benefits by 2035 and a 75% reduction could generate $45bn. These numbers are no prescription to slash prices; rather, they must be weighed against the state’s undeniable fiscal duty to manage a public asset.
At the same time, operators need capital for advanced radios and network upgrades. The real policy challenge is not finding an arbitrary, magic price per megahertz, but ensuring that every megahertz becomes highly productive.
Spectrum productivity is best measured by its capacity for dense urban hubs, wider coverage for rural villages, and reliable network quality during peak hours. Yet, BTRC data exposes a deep structural imbalance in our airwaves.
State-owned Teletalk holds 65.2 MHz for just 6.8 million subscribers, while Grameenphone must squeeze 84.4 million subscribers into 137.4 MHz. Serving remote terrain explains part of this gap, but not all of it.
When rigid frameworks lock spectrum in underutilized silos while urban networks suffer from congestion, the scarcity becomes artificial. Because traffic patterns shift constantly, a band that was adequate five years ago may leave one city congested today while sitting idle in another. If frequency blocks cannot move dynamically to match this shifting public demand, the consumer experience inevitably degrades, and the broader digital economy suffers.
Other nations have long recognized that draining an operator's capital through high upfront spectrum fees may starve the investments needed for network rollouts. Many have shifted toward models that trade immediate financial burdens for guaranteed socio-economic outcomes.
India addressed artificial scarcity by legalizing spectrum trading and sharing , allowing rights to move toward operators facing heavy traffic. Its framework permitted transfers subject to spectrum caps, roll-out obligations, eligibility conditions and a two-year holding period, with a 1% transfer fee.
Similarly, Austria and Colombia tied their low-band spectrum licensing directly to rural coverage, allowing operators to earn explicit fee discounts or convert coverage commitments into cash-equivalent credits. Spain and Canada chose to extend license terms or waive upfront renewal fees where operators could demonstrate minimum population coverage , giving companies the necessary breathing room to amortize massive hardware investments.
The warnings from the global markets should also be watched closely. In its multi-band auction, Pakistan cut reserve prices on legacy bands by more than 50%, yet those bands still drew no bids.
This proved that artificial benchmarks fail to create demand for spectrum that lacks commercial viability. In contrast, Vietnam demonstrates the power of flexible strategic asset pricing; after a failed 2023 auction, it slashed reserve prices by nearly 80%, separating long-term economic utility from the temptation of short-term cash extraction to rapidly achieve roughly 90% 5G coverage by early 2026.
Meanwhile, other regulatory experiments show distinct operational challenges: Austria faced ambiguity over how coverage would be measured. Colombia’s process was criticized for hiding minimum bids in advance while miscalculating rural rollout costs.
Finally, Canada’s model serves as a direct warning; its rigid obligation conditions drove up holding costs without incentivizing efficient use, creating long-term operational inefficiencies after the regulator ignored industry challenges during consultations.
To break out of the cycle of revenue-maximizing deadlocks and deteriorating network quality, Bangladesh needs a pragmatic, forward-looking approach. Rather than exhausting operator liquidity through high upfront hurdles, BTRC can incentivize infrastructure development by recalibrating its renewal fees into a more manageable, back-loaded payment timeline.
Dr Sabbir Ahmad is a tech executive with global experience in digital connectivity, sustainable infrastructure and energy. He is shaping Bangladesh's semiconductor landscape as the CEO of Silicon Array Ltd. Email: sabbir@ieee.org .

Two shot, school student stabbed in Badda
item.description:
Three people, including two who suffered gunshot wounds, were injured in separate shooting and stabbing incidents in the capital’s Badda area on Monday night.
The injured were identified as Md Al-Amin, 25, and Saiful Islam, 23, who sustained gunshot wounds, and Abdullah, 16, a school student who was stabbed.
Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Selim Hossain of the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) police outpost confirmed the incidents and said the injured received treatment at DMCH on Monday night.
Kawsar Tarek, Abdullah’s maternal uncle, said Abdullah and several friends were passing by Alatunnesa School in Badda around 10pm when unidentified assailants stabbed him on the street.
“I heard there had been a clash between two groups there shortly before the incident. Later, members of one group attacked people they encountered on the street,” he said.
Abdullah, an SSC examinee, is a student at a local school and lives in Madhya Badda.
Earlier, Al-Amin was shot during a clash between two groups in the area. His friend Russell, who took him to the hospital, said Al-Amin lives behind Alatunnesa School.
Al-Amin was shot in the right knee while passing through the area and was later rescued and taken to hospital.
Around 11pm, Saiful Islam, a refrigerator mechanic, was shot in the leg in an alley near Merul Badda Bazar.
Saiful, who lives at Mondal residence in the Badda Bazar area, was returning home when two helmeted assailants attempted to stop him.
As he tried to flee, they allegedly fired at him from behind, hitting him in the leg.
A neighbour, Mohan Gazi, rescued him and took him to hospital.
Badda police station Duty Officer SI Md Abu Zafar said two incidents occurred within the station’s jurisdiction and that legal proceedings had been initiated.
“Police officers are working on the cases, and efforts are underway to arrest those involved,” he said.

item.title: Man hacked to death in Tongi
item.description:
A 23-year-old man was hacked to death by unidentified assailants in Tongi, Gazipur, police said.
The victim, Joy, was the son of Sirajul Islam and lived in the Bank Math slum area of Tongi.
The incident occurred around 1am on Monday near Tongi Railway Station.
According to police, Joy was returning home when several youths attacked him with sharp weapons and fled the scene after killing him.
Local residents witnessed the incident and informed the Tongi Railway Police Outpost. Police recovered the body and sent it to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy.
No one has been detained in connection with the killing, and the motive has not yet been established, police said.
However, preliminary investigations suggest that the killing may have stemmed from a previous dispute.
Police are examining CCTV footage from the area to identify those involved.
Nur Alam Hossain, in-charge and a sub-inspector at the Tongi Railway Police Outpost, said a murder case would be filed with Kamalapur Railway Police Station in Dhaka over the incident.

HC orders BB to release funds for 4 National Bank clients
item.description:
The High Court has directed Bangladesh Bank to ensure that four depositors of National Bank PLC can withdraw funds from their savings accounts, following allegations that the lender repeatedly refused to release their money without valid grounds.
An interim order was issued Monday by a High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice Md. Ali Reza at Annex Court No. 29. The order came following the hearing of Writ Petition No. 13668/2026, titled Lucky Akter and Others v. Bangladesh and Others, which was listed at serial number 174 on the day's cause list.
Along with the interim directive, the court issued a rule asking the respondents why a direction should not be given to allow the petitioners to withdraw their legally deposited funds. The respondents include the Ministry of Finance, Bangladesh Bank and its relevant officials, and National Bank PLC.
Under the interim order, the central bank—represented by its Governor, General Manager, and the Directors of the Technology Risk and Digital Banking Supervision Department and the Customer Interest Protection Center (CIPC)—must take necessary regulatory actions based on the complaints. They are required to ensure that National Bank allows the four petitioners to draw their money. Supreme Court advocate Maruf-ul-Abed represented the petitioners and confirmed the order via a lawyer's certificate issued the same day.
All four petitioners hold savings accounts with National Bank. Lucky Akter maintains an account at the Mirzapur SME Krishi Branch in Tangail; Nasima Begum and Mst. Sathi Begum hold accounts at the Mirzapur Branch; and Md. Shamim Ahmed is an account holder at the Bhaluka Branch in Mymensingh. Shamim Ahmed also represents the other petitioners under a power of attorney dated September 20, 2026.
According to the writ petition, the issue arose on September 17 when the four customers visited their respective branches to encash checks. Branch officials refused to accept the checks or disburse the cash without providing any valid or satisfactory reason. Among them, Nasima Begum was denied withdrawal despite presenting a check for BDT 30,000.
The petition stated that the accounts are active, valid, and show sufficient credit balances. Despite repeated visits to the branches, the customers were denied their money without any legal order or written explanation. Having failed to get redress from the bank, they submitted written complaints via email to Bangladesh Bank’s CIPC and the Financial Integrity and Customer Services Department (FICSD), but received no resolution.
Describing themselves as low- and middle-income individuals, the petitioners stated that they rely on these savings for daily necessities, medical treatment, and education. Withholding deposited funds without legal authority violates fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution, including equality before the law (Article 27), protection of law (Article 31), protection of life and personal liberty (Article 32), and property rights (Article 42). They emphasized that they were not seeking special favors, but simply demanding their money in accordance with the law. The petition added that resolving such grievances falls under the statutory duty of Bangladesh Bank as the regulator of scheduled banks, and its failure to act is challengeable under Article 102 of the Constitution.
The court order comes amid an ongoing liquidity crisis at National Bank. In February this year ahead of Eid, the lender received BDT 1,000 crore in emergency liquidity support from Bangladesh Bank as it struggled to honor customer withdrawals.
The bank's asset quality has also degraded significantly. As of March 31, 2026, its defaulted loans rose to BDT 24,302 crore, accounting for 56.44 percent of its total disbursed loans.
A report by The media highlighted severe hardships faced by customers nationwide, with branches rationing cash and ATM booths frequently running dry. The acting managing director of the bank told the daily that news of the emergency support inadvertently triggered a fresh panic among depositors, forcing management to systematically restrict daily cash payouts.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,099 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,099.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 998, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the three new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Chittagong division, with two deaths. At the district level, one casualty each was recorded in Chittagong, Noakhali, and Sylhet.
A total of 1,214 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 189,255.
During the same period, 96 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,308.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 167,469 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 160,705 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Salauddin: No journalist to be victimized under Cyber Security law
item.description:
The government is exercising utmost caution so that the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act does not become an oppressive law and that no journalist or media outlet is victimized under it, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Monday.
The proposed law would be finalized only after extensive consultations with stakeholders and consideration of their recommendations, he said at a press briefing at the Secretariat following a consultation meeting with representatives of print and electronic media at the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
“Our primary objective is to ensure that no journalist falls victim to the misuse of this law,” he said.
The home minister said the draft amendment bill was earlier laid before the Cabinet, which directed the authorities to hold extensive discussions with IT experts and other stakeholders involved in cyberspace.
Then the government published the draft on its website to seek opinions from people from all walks of life, he said, adding that feedback has already been received from various institutions, human rights organisations, students and cyberspace users.
Monday’s meeting was the government’s second consultation with editors, senior journalists, newspaper organisations and representatives of professional journalists’ associations.
At the first meeting on September 10, editors were requested to submit their views in writing or through the website.
The minister said many participants presented their views at Monday’s meeting and pledged to submit written recommendations.
He said a proposal came to hold detailed discussions between media and cyber experts to ensure that the media is not harmed or victimised and that necessary safeguards are incorporated into the law.
“The government has gladly accepted the proposal,” Salahuddin said, adding that the government has no intention of enacting the law to target the media.
Regarding safeguards for journalists in print, electronic and online media, the minister said a proposal was made to make prior court approval mandatory before taking action against or arresting a journalist.
He said the government considered the proposal appropriate and logical.
Stakeholders will be given another 15 days to submit formal recommendations, which will then be considered for inclusion in the draft, he said.
A provision setting a specific timeframe for the disposal of cases or appeals will also be considered to prevent people from remaining in legal uncertainty for an indefinite period, the minister added.
Salahuddin said a special coordination mechanism would be formed to help finalise the draft.
The Principal Information Officer will serve as the focal point, while the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting will jointly coordinate the process.
Representatives of the Editors’ Council, Electronic Media Association and a panel of cyber experts formed by the IT ministry will participate in the process and are expected to submit recommendations within 7 to 15 days, said the minister.
The revised draft will then be published on the government website again for further public feedback before being placed before the Cabinet, the minister added.
If the recommendations are accepted, they will be incorporated into the draft before an inter-ministerial review and submission to the Cabinet.
After Cabinet approval, the bill will be placed before Parliament where it will undergo further deliberation involving members of both the ruling and opposition parties as well as views emerging from seminars and symposiums outside Parliament.
Salahuddin said the main objective of the proposed law is to establish a balanced legal framework to protect the country, society and young people from cybercrimes and other criminal activities.
The act is also intended to comply with international standards while protecting social and religious harmony, family values and indigenous culture, he said.

item.title: State minister: No hidden agenda behind Boeing deal
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Monday said there is no hidden agenda behind the latest agreement with Boeing, reiterating that Bangladesh will continue to expand Biman’s fleet based on needs as the country eyes becoming an aviation hub.
"We need to expand the fleet to become an aviation hub. There is nothing....there is no hidden agenda. Bangladesh does it on the basis of needs. We need to expand our fleet," he told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs while responding to a question.
Kobir laid emphasis on a mixed fleet in the interest of the country’s aviation sector.
The state minister described the just-concluded visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the 81st session of the UNGA as "successful and meaningful," with extensive engagements with the international community during his four-day stay in New York.
Kobir said the speech of the prime minister at the UNGA was highly appreciated by the international community.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the country's national flag carrier, signed an agreement with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to acquire 11 additional aircraft during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
"Congratulations to Boeing and Biman on the agreement to purchase 11 more of the world’s best commercial planes. Another win-win for the US-Bangladesh relationship! Will be tuning in to the signing ceremony in New York later," said US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T Christensen moments before the signing ceremony.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to buy 14 planes for its national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the two sides announced - the airline’s biggest-ever order, in a deal valued at $3.7 billion.

item.title: 4,585 SSC, equivalent exam candidates pass after re-scrutiny
item.description:
A total of 4,585 candidates who initially failed the SSC and equivalent examinations in 2026 have passed after their answer scripts were re-scrutinised and re-evaluated.
In addition, 3,079 candidates received new GPAs.
The Ministry of Education released the statistics on the results of the re-scrutiny and re-evaluation on Monday.
According to ministry data, a total of 1,829,485 candidates appeared for the SSC and equivalent examinations. Of them, 402,052 candidates applied for re-scrutiny and re-evaluation of their answer scripts.
Among the answer scripts submitted for review, 1,056,455 were theoretical scripts and 231,471 were practical scripts. A total of 1,287,926 scripts were re-scrutinised.
The results showed grade changes for 27,836 candidates, while the marks of 56,259 candidates were changed.

item.title: Embassy issues travel advisory for Bangladeshis visiting Nepal
item.description:
The Embassy of Bangladesh in Kathmandu on Sunday night urged Bangladeshi tourists and trekkers to exercise caution while travelling in Nepal amid heavy rainfall, floods and landslides.
The embassy advised travellers to avoid visiting affected areas until weather conditions and the overall situation improve.
It urged particular caution in tourist destinations including Pisang, Chame, Manang and surrounding areas, where continuous rainfall has triggered landslides and snowfall, disrupting road connectivity in several locations. Rescue operations have also been hampered by the rugged terrain and disrupted transport links.
Authorities have suspended trekking activities in several parts of Manang, including routes to Tilicho Lake, Thorong La Pass, Ice Lake, Kang La and Bhimthang.
Travellers have also been advised to exercise caution while visiting Pokhara and surrounding areas, as landslides have disrupted road links and access to nearby trekking destinations.
Those planning to travel to Mustang, Jomsom and other mountainous areas have been advised to check road conditions in Gandaki Province, where routes can be disrupted suddenly.
Bangladeshi citizens planning trekking, mountaineering or travel in mountainous and landslide-prone areas, including Annapurna, Manang, Mustang and Manaslu, have been advised to verify travel information and strictly follow directives issued by the Nepal government and local authorities.
Bangladeshi citizens already in areas vulnerable to such hazards have been advised to stay in safe locations, avoid riverbanks and landslide-prone areas, check road and weather conditions before travelling, and remain in regular contact with their travel operators and the embassy.
The embassy said it is monitoring the situation in coordination with Nepali authorities and will issue further updates as necessary.

item.title: 8 held over alleged vandalism, looting in Mohammadpur land dispute
item.description:
Police have arrested eight people for allegedly vandalizing an office and looting valuables in an attempt to take control of a property in the Satmasjid Housing area of Mohammadpur, Dhaka.
Mohammadpur police confirmed the arrests.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Deputy Commissioner (Media and Public Relations) Md Akter Hossain confirmed the matter on Monday.
Police could not immediately provide the identities of those arrested.
The incident took place around 10am on Saturday at Chand Udyan Housing in the Beribadh area of Mohammadpur.
Zainal Abedin, who described himself as a victim of the incident, submitted a written complaint to Mohammadpur police station.
According to the complaint, around 100-150 unidentified people allegedly entered the second-floor office of Mohammadpur Twin Tower after breaking its doors, locks and windows.
They allegedly searched several rooms and a storeroom before taking Tk15 lakh in cash, five laptops, two air conditioners, three CCTV cameras, office furniture and other equipment. The items were allegedly loaded onto a truck.
Zainal alleged that Md Mostak Rahman Khokon Chowdhury, 62, along with Mohin, Prince and Alamin and the assistance of several local individuals, had been attempting to take control of the office for some time.
The complaint said the incident caused financial losses to the organization and raised concerns over the loss of important official documents and information.
It further alleged that the incident disrupted the office's normal operations and caused significant financial and administrative losses.

item.title: Five arrested over attack on house in Adabor
item.description:
Five people have been arrested in connection with an attack on a house in the Shyamoli Housing area of Adabor in the capital.
Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division, Md Akter Hossain, confirmed the matter at around 11:15am on Monday.
The DMP said five people were arrested in connection with the attack on a house in the Shyamoli Housing area of Adabor. The DMP did not immediately disclose the names or identities of those arrested.
The attack on the house in Adabor took place on Saturday morning. A group of 15 to 20 people, armed with machetes, cleavers and a pistol, allegedly carried out the attack. It has been alleged that an attempt was being made to take control of the eight-storey house.
The owner of the house, Aminur Rahman Khan, is a businessman. His nephew, Monir Hossain, said the house had also been occupied once after August 5, 2024.
Following Saturday’s incident, the house owner, Aminur Rahman, filed a case with Adabor Police Station on Sunday night.
The case names Khurshid Alam Khan, Habibullah alias Russell, Kalam, Kamran Hossain, Mizanur Rahman, Sajib Hossain, Hasibul Hasan alias Emon, Tanvir and 15–20 others as accused. The remaining individuals have been listed as unidentified.

item.title: Gold prices drop further
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has reduced gold prices again, with the price of 22-carat gold falling by Tk185 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold will cost Tk19,785 per gram, including VAT.
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Monday, following another reduction announced by Bajus on Saturday.
The Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring set the new rates at a meeting at 9am on Monday. The decision was announced in a notification signed by the committee’s chairman, Dr Dewan Aminul Islam Shahin.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk230,770, including VAT. Making charges will be added separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
The price of 21-carat gold has been set at Tk18,895 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,225 per gram. Gold sold under the traditional method has been priced at Tk13,225 per gram.
On September 26, the price of 22-carat gold stood at Tk19,970 per gram, including VAT. The price per bhori was reduced by Tk1,691 that day.
With Monday’s reduction, the price of 22-carat gold has fallen by approximately Tk2,159 per bhori over two days.
Bajus has also reduced the prices of silver jewellery.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver will cost Tk385 per gram, 21-carat silver Tk370, 18-carat silver Tk320 and traditional-method silver Tk240 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk415 per gram on September 26, meaning it has fallen by Tk30 per gram in two days.
Bajus said making charges will be applicable separately based on the design of the jewellery.
However, as VAT is already included in the fixed selling price, it cannot be charged separately from customers.
For exchanges involving old gold jewellery, 12% will be deducted from the gold price, excluding making charges and the cost of stones. For purchases of old jewellery, the deduction will be 18%.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either exchange or purchase transactions, according to Bajus.
The new rates will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
Bajus said the decision was taken after reviewing the overall market situation, including a decline in the prices of raw gold and silver.

item.title: Milestone man Kohli's 139 powers India to big ODI win over West Indies
item.description:
Virat Kohli hit a record-extending 55th one-day international century after reaching 15,000 runs to lead India to a dominant eight-wicket win over the West Indies in the series opener on Sunday.
Kohli, who hit an unbeaten 139, put on 151 runs for the second wicket with skipper Shubman Gill (110) as India chased down their victory target of 296 with 50 balls to spare in Thiruvananthapuram.
Kohli hit the winning six -- the ninth in his 88-ball knock -- as India went 1-0 up in the three-match series, which is a step in the team's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup.
The 37-year-old Kohli made the evening his own as he went past 15,000 ODI runs to become only the second batter after icon Sachin Tendulkar to achieve the feat.
"My focus has never really been on these milestones," said Kohli.
"It's just understanding the situation along the course of just doing the job for the team. Achievements come along. Obviously, I feel very grateful and very blessed to be in this position for having played for so long."
Kohli reached the milestone with a boundary in his 303rd ODI innings, while Tendulkar, who finished his illustrious career with 18,426 runs, took 377 innings to get to 15,000.
Gill reached his 10th ODI hundred but the spotlight soon shifted back to Kohli, who reached his 100 with a six as a raucous home crowd stood up to applaud the star cricketer.
The top-order batter is leading century-maker in ODIs with Tendulkar next with 49 hundreds. Rohit Sharma is third with 34 tons.
Kohli and the 39-year-old Rohit are both playing only in the 50-over format after their Test and T20 retirements, as they look ahead to the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
"We're a year away from the World Cup. I know what my goal is, and yeah, it's pretty clear for me that whatever games we get, I just need to keep working on different aspects of the game," said Kohli.
"Keep myself physically fit, challenge myself to be out there, run from boundary to boundary in the last 15 overs if I can, field in the inner ring, show intensity."
Kohli on Saturday told broadcasters JioStar that the 2027 showpiece would be his last World Cup appearance.
Rohit got the team off to a brisk start in his 32 as he put on 74 with opening partner Gill.
Earlier, Justin Greaves made 101 and put on 135 for the first wicket with left-hander John Campbell, who made 62, to guide West Indies to 295-7.
Left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav struck crucial blows to return figures of 4-40 including one maiden over as India hit back in the middle overs.
Kuldeep, who was named player of the match, also struck on successive balls, sending back Greaves and Jewel Andrew before Roston Chase avoided the hat-trick.
Chase steadied the innings with Amir Jangoo, who made an unbeaten 58, as the pair put on 52 for the sixth wicket.
The second ODI is on Wednesday in Guwahati.

item.title: Why India’s opposition wants top poll official out
item.description:
The Election Commission of India, long regarded as the guardian of the world’s largest democracy, is facing scrutiny after a newspaper investigation alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision.
According to an Indian Express report last week, some key decisions linked to the contentious revision exercise were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.
The ECI, a constitutional body, has rejected the allegations, saying all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid.
Opposition parties have long raised doubts about the nationwide revision, which has seen millions of names removed from voter rolls, saying it benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
Here is a rundown of the major issues at stake:
The English-language daily reported that the poll body had been riven by internal disagreements since the so-called Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter lists started last year.
It said two of the ECI’s three commissioners formally lodged objections at least 14 times in the last 10 months over key SIR decisions that led to the omission of 130 million voters.
Under India’s constitution, decisions by the three-member poll body should be taken by consensus or a majority.
The ECI says the SIR exercise is intended to identify fraudulently registered voters while ensuring those who are eligible remain on the rolls.
It also says the exercise aims to prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from voting.
But critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalized and minority communities.
Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.
The ECI has denied the central allegation that decisions were taken unilaterally by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
“All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” it said in a statement on Wednesday.
The allegations reported by The Indian Express presented “only one part of the picture,” and “differing views” were a routine “part of decision-making,” it added.
The ECI has not publicly explained who authorized the specific orders that the two commissioners had challenged.
Opposition parties are demanding Kumar’s resignation and a Supreme Court-led investigation into the matter.
They are also seeking an independent probe into the Election Commission’s functioning as well as the voter-roll revision.
“If decisions relating to the SIR were taken without the knowledge or approval of two of the three Election Commissioners... then those decisions and the entire SIR exercise are legally invalid,” Pawan Khera of the main opposition Congress party said on social media.
“Gyanesh Kumar has done nothing short of treason.”
The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party has also threatened to hit the streets from October 2 -- the birth anniversary of India’s founding father Mahatma Gandhi -- if Kumar does not resign.
The online movement, which has millions of followers on social media, forced education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign in July, following widespread student-led street protests.

item.title: Death toll in South Africa bar shooting rises to 18
item.description:
The death toll in a mass shooting in a South African tavern has risen to 18 after one person died in hospital, police said Monday, adding that at least two of the dead were Lesotho nationals.
The shooting west of Johannesburg late Saturday was part of a bloody weekend in the crime-weary country, with 10 people killed in another mass shooting in Cape Town on Sunday.
Eight gunmen armed with assault rifles stormed the bar in the semi-rural township of Wedela, around 80 kilometers (50 miles) from central Johannesburg, killing 13 men and four women, police said.
“One more victim has died in hospital, bringing the total number of deceased to 18,” they said Monday. Eighteen people were wounded.
“Only four of the deceased have been identified, two South Africans and two Lesotho nationals.”
The motive for the attack was not clear, but police said it may have been retaliation for an incident in the same tavern in August when one person was killed and another wounded.
The area was gripped by rivalry between gangs involved in illicit mining for gold, the tavern owner told local journalists at the scene, where bloodied clothes lay on the ground.
“Even if they finish investigating, I am scared to continue selling again. I am too scared,” she said, hiding her identity.
Thousands of unregistered miners operate in abandoned mining shafts in South Africa, in a sector linked to organized crime, assassinations and other illegal activities.
Many come from across southern Africa, including the kingdom of Lesotho which is embedded within South Africa.
In a separate shooting at the weekend, gunmen killed 10 people and wounded 11 more at an eating and drinking venue in a township outside Cape Town early on Sunday.
In video clips shared on social media, revelers can be seen dancing and drinking before a burst of gunfire rings out, sending people scrambling for cover.
Police said it was not clear what prompted the attack in Lwandle, but one official said it may have been business rivalry.
There had been no arrests in either of the mass killings.
South Africa is awash with legal and illegal firearms and shootings are common. The country of around 62 million people has one of the world’s highest murder rates, with about 60 people killed each day.
There have been at least 41 mass killings this year at the cost of 196 lives, said Julian Rademeyer, an adviser for the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC).
“Very often these are killings that are linked to organized crime” including illegal mining, gang violence and extortion, he told the Newzroom Afrika broadcaster.
In March, President Cyril Ramaphosa deployed the army to violence hotspots around Johannesburg and Cape Town after describing organized crime the “most immediate threat” to South Africa’s democracy and economic development.
The weekend bloodshed further rattled South Africans already alarmed by the discovery of the bodies of 11 women, one of them on Sunday, in 10 weeks in Johannesburg’s Ekurhuleni area.
Most of the victims were in their 20s and 30s, with some found stripped of their clothes and showing signs of sexual assault, police said.
In the same area, a 23-year-old woman was shot and killed early Monday during an alleged robbery while she was on the way to work, police said.
“Preliminary investigations have not established any link between this incident and the recent cases involving the bodies of women found in Ekurhuleni,” they said in a statement.

item.title: Tolls mount in Thailand, Myanmar floods
item.description:
Heavy rains have killed eight people in Thailand since mid-September, the government said Monday as Bangkok battled flooding for a fourth consecutive day, with at least eight more confirmed dead in neighboring Myanmar.
The casualties in Thailand have occurred in three eastern provinces since September 16, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation, with none reported in the capital.
More than 500,000 households and 1.7 million people across 27 provinces are currently affected by floods in Thailand after an intense weather system hit the region, it said.
In hard-hit Bangkok, schools were closed and authorities urged people to work from home where possible -- a call that many heeded, with roads and public transport networks noticeably quieter.
More than 80,000 people were unable to leave their homes in the capital due to flooding, the interior ministry said.
Nattapon Mankean, 32, said his apartment complex in Bang Kapi, eastern Bangkok, had no electricity or water, so he and his girlfriend fled with two cats, one in a cage and the other in a specialized rucksack.
“Our phone batteries died, we had no running water -- everything became difficult,” the 32-year-old told AFP late on Sunday.
“It was terrible, I couldn’t do anything,” he added. “I had to get out.”
Authorities declared a city-wide disaster on Saturday after almost 48 hours of heavy rain, and on Monday some residents were still wading through thigh-high waters.
In Bang Kapi locals used ice-boxes and other floating plastic containers to cart supplies from nearby markets and supermarkets, AFP reporters saw.
The rains that lashed Thailand also hit neighboring Myanmar, where rescuers said heavy floods and landslides in the southern region of Tanintharyi had killed at least eight people.
“We have recovered eight bodies while between 20 to 30 people are missing” in Launglon township, said Hein Htet, of the local volunteer group People’s Administration Team.
Three of the recovered bodies were teenagers who had gathered at a local monastery on Sunday but were swept away by a landslide that hit their village, burying 18 buildings, he said.
“There are still people and villages in the danger zone with continued rainfall,” he warned.
Myanmar’s civil war often makes the scale of natural disasters hard for humanitarian organizations to judge, as well as complicating relief efforts.
“We are inundated not only with the scale of the flood but also with the lack of resources. This is a natural disaster in the conflict area,” said Hein Htet.
September is the peak of Thailand’s rainy season, but many Bangkok residents said this year’s floods seemed worse than previous ones.
The city is built on former marshlands and is intersected by a network of canals, many of them heavily flooded by the rains.
Pumping stations have been operating at full capacity for days, but Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said Sunday it could take “up to a week” for the waters to fully drain.
Thousands of residents have decamped to temporary shelters.
In a briefing on Monday, government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said floods were receding, but “some areas in Bangkok are still facing high water levels.”
“I was so shocked, things happened so quickly,” said Samran, a retired company worker whose building was flooded.
“My flat’s car park was under water -- it never floods, even in 2011” when hundreds of people died across Thailand in heavy deluges, he said, asking AFP not to publish his family name.
“I have drinking water but I do not have water for my toilet,” he said, saying he had to use a bucket to pull water up through the window to his second-floor apartment.
Scientists warn the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as global warming accelerates because of fossil fuel emissions.

item.title: Trump offered to sell arms to Xi
item.description:
US President Donald Trump offered to sell arms to his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in response to concern over weapons sales to Taiwan, the US ambassador to China said in a Fox News interview that aired Sunday.
US arms sales to the self-ruled island, which China claims is part of its territory and has threatened to seize by force, have long been a thorny issue between Washington and Beijing.
The United States is required by law to supply Taiwan, which has a democratically elected president and legislature, with weapons for its defense.
US Ambassador to China David Perdue said the issue was raised again when Xi visited the United States last week.
“President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.’ He actually asked President Xi -- would he like to buy some? -- at one point,” Perdue said in the interview.
“There are continuing conversations about other sales, (Trump) and President Xi talk about that every time they get together,” Perdue said, adding that the US position has not changed.
The White House did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment.
White House officials said that the US had no plans to sell arms to China, according to the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal.
The US State Department said in a statement to the New York Times that “US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.”
The Chinese foreign ministry did not directly answer when asked about the comments on Monday, but said China has “always strengthened its national defense capabilities based on its own needs, and remains committed to maintaining world peace and stability.”
Beijing warned Taiwan in June that seeking independence “by relying on the United States or through military means is a dead end.”
Washington approved a $11.1 billion arms sale to Taiwan in December, which Perdue said was a sale of “more arms to Taiwan than any other president since 1979.”
The US paused a $14 billion weapons purchase by Taiwan in May, with Trump calling it a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China, raising fears that Taiwan’s security could be traded away.
During his Washington trip, Xi repeated his warning that Trump should show “prudence” over Taiwan, and went further to urge the United States to oppose Taiwan independence explicitly.
Both leaders confirmed they would meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami in December.

Speakers: Workers’ demands should be reflected in COP31 position paper
item.description:
Workers’ rights, social protection, workplace safety, decent work, skills development and climate resilience should be reflected in Bangladesh’s position paper for the upcoming UN climate conference COP31, speakers said at a workshop in the capital on Sunday.
They said climate change is already affecting workers through heat stress, reduced working hours, unsafe workplaces and livelihood risks, making workers’ priorities an essential part of the country’s just transition agenda.
The remarks came at the “Workshop on Worker Position Paper for COP31”, held at After Hours Residence in Banani.
Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) and the National Alliance for Just Transition Bangladesh (NAJTB) organized the workshop with support from Oxfam and Bangladesh Labour Foundation (BLF), the joint secretariat of NAJTB. Bangladesh Institute of Labour Studies (BILS), a member of NAJTB, also participated.
The workshop was organized under MJF’s Fashion Forward project, through which the human rights-based organization is working to support a fair, inclusive and worker-responsive transition in the apparel sector.
Speakers said the workshop was part of a series of consultations. The next consultations will involve youth and government stakeholders, following which the recommendations will be consolidated and aligned with the government’s COP31 position paper for final submission.
Elisa Benistant Fremigacci, technical officer, Just Transitions, ILO Bangladesh, said COP31 is being framed as the “COP of implementation” and workers in Bangladesh must push for policy commitments to be translated into action.
She stressed the need for dedicated financing, meaningful dialogue, direct representation and accountability in implementing the just transition chapter of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
Participants attend a workshop on the Worker Position Paper for COP31 at After Hours Residence in Banani on Sunday, September 27, 2026. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Md Muhtasim Billah, senior program officer at Oxfam Bangladesh, said a just transition should not focus solely on the shift in energy systems.
“It must safeguard workers’ rights, ensure social protection and secure decent work standards across sectors,” he said.
AKM Ashraf Uddin, executive director of BLF and member secretary of NAJTB, said the direct participation of worker and employer representatives in COP negotiations was a major step forward.
He said NAJTB, which brings together nearly 60 civil society and trade union organisations across around 20 sectors, is preparing a unified Workers’ Charter of Demands for COP31.
Presenting the keynote, Mir Mohammad Ali, assistant professor at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, said extreme heatwaves and climate hazards were causing serious losses to workers and the economy.
He recommended incorporating the Workers’ Charter into the government’s position paper, including provisions for paid heat-rest breaks, social security, skills development and worker representation in the official delegation.
Zubaer Alam, program officer at BLF, said youth groups, trade unions and government committees would be engaged by mid-October to prepare a grounded Workers’ Position Paper.
Pablo Narudha, Project Coordinator of Fashion Forward at MJF, said MJF had worked with workers for more than two decades to protect their fundamental rights and that workers’ priorities should be reflected in national climate policy.
Wasiur Rahman Tonmoy, lead, Youth and Social Cohesion at MJF, said workers’ voices needed to be reflected in clear, evidence-based and actionable language.
He said MJF would continue to promote human rights through worker-led evidence, youth engagement and policy advocacy.
Syed Sultan Uddin Ahmed, executive coordinator of NAJTB and executive director of BILS, also emphasized the need to incorporate workers’ demands into the COP31 position paper.
Representatives from trade unions, civil society organizations, development partners and other stakeholders attended the workshop.

item.title: Cox’s Bazar’s tourism boom comes at a cost
item.description:
Millions of tourists flock to Cox’s Bazar each year to enjoy its iconic sea beach, but growing commercial activity, traffic congestion, waste and inadequate facilities are increasingly affecting the visitor experience.
At the Laboni, Sugandha and Kalatali points, rows of temporary shops, street vendors, beach bikes, horses, photographers and other commercial activities have become a familiar sight.
For some visitors, the growing presence of vendors and businesses is taking away from the tranquillity of the beach.
“Within a few minutes of entering the beach, different vendors start approaching us,” said Lovely Akter, who visited Cox’s Bazar from Dhaka with her family.
“We came to enjoy the sea, but we have to listen to business offers repeatedly,” she said.
Tourist couple Sohel Mazhar and Shiuli, who travelled from Rajshahi, also complained about the quality and cost of services.
Millions of tourists come to Cox’s Bazar to enjoy the sea beach, but services have not improved at the same pace, they said. Commercial activities are everywhere, and prices often seem excessive. The authorities need to pay greater attention to this.
During peak tourism seasons, traffic congestion is a regular problem in Kalatali, Sugandha and Jhautala. Unplanned parking, footpath encroachment and increasing traffic volumes make movement difficult for tourists and local residents alike.
Tourism stakeholders say the growth in visitor numbers has not been matched by adequate improvements in infrastructure and urban management.
Environmentalists are also concerned about the impact of unregulated activities and increasing tourist pressure on the beach ecosystem.
Dipak Sharma Dipu, president of the Cox’s Bazar Forest and Environment Journalists’ Council, said the sea, sandy beach and natural environment are the destination’s most important assets.
“Unplanned commercial activities, noise pollution, plastic waste and other uncontrolled activities are gradually damaging the beach environment,” he said.
Plastic bottles, food wrappers and other waste are frequently found on different parts of the beach, he said, adding that such waste not only affects the area’s beauty but could also pose a threat to marine biodiversity.
Local businesses say tourism-related commercial activities are also an important source of livelihood for thousands of people.
Mohammad Abdullah, manager of Beach Bangla Tourism in Cox’s Bazar, said vendors, small traders, photographers, transport workers and hotel and restaurant employees all depend on the tourism economy.
“Thousands of people depend on tourism for their livelihoods,” he said. “The solution is not to stop business activities, but to ensure that they are properly regulated and managed.”
Tourism stakeholders say designated commercial zones, improved waste management, better parking facilities and long-term traffic management could help balance commercial interests with the needs of tourists and the environment.
Moukhim Khan, general secretary of the Kalatali-Marine Drive Road Hotel-Motel Owners’ Association, said Cox’s Bazar needs better facilities and international-standard events to attract tourists throughout the year.
“Regular government-organised fairs and other events could help attract tourists year-round,” he said. “At the same time, the quality of tourist services must be improved.”
Abu Morshed Chowdhury Khoka, president of Cox’s Bazar Civil Society, said environmental protection must remain a priority alongside tourism development.
“The natural beauty of Cox’s Bazar is important not only for tourists but also for the national economy,” he said. “If the openness, aesthetic appeal and natural environment of the beach are not protected, it could eventually affect tourists’ interest in the destination.”
Cox’s Bazar Deputy Commissioner Md Abdul Mannan said the government has taken initiatives to promote sustainable tourism and improve tourist safety, cleanliness and modern facilities.
“A master plan is being prepared to develop sustainable tourism and attract foreign tourists,” he said.
He said initiatives were also being taken to restore order on the beach, ensure cleanliness, remove illegal encroachments and improve tourist safety.
Meanwhile, a three-day tourism fair has been organized in Cox’s Bazar to mark World Tourism Day, which promotes sustainable, environmentally friendly and people-centred tourism.
For Cox’s Bazar, the message is particularly relevant. The city’s tourism economy depends fundamentally on the natural beauty of its coastline. Managing commercial activity, protecting the environment and improving public services will therefore remain central to the destination’s long-term tourism prospects.
As the number of visitors continues to grow, the challenge for Cox’s Bazar is to ensure that tourism development does not come at the expense of the very natural environment that attracts tourists in the first place.

item.title: Schoolgirl hacked to death: Accused sentenced to death after 19 years
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Sunday sentenced Rezaul Islam to death for killing seventh-grade student Mahmuda Akter Roxi in Ashulia, Savar, in 2007 after she rejected his marriage proposal.
Judge Md Humayun Kabir of the 3rd Additional District and Sessions Judge’s Court in Dhaka delivered the verdict. The court also directed the relevant police superintendent to take measures to arrest the fugitive convict and enforce the sentence.
Bench assistant Md Aminur Rahman confirmed the matter.
According to the case details and court sources, Rezaul proposed marriage to Roxi, a fatherless orphan student from Ashulia, on March 28, 2007. After she rejected the proposal, Rezaul allegedly threatened and intimidated her.
On the morning of April 2, 2007, Rezaul entered Roxi’s room and repeatedly struck her on the head with a spade. The attack fractured her skull into 3 pieces and exposed her brain.
Roxi was rescued in critical condition and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where she died that night while undergoing treatment.
Following the incident, Roxi’s maternal cousin Nurul Islam Babu filed a murder case with Ashulia police station.
After completing the investigation, Ashulia Police Station Sub-Inspector Alim Uddin submitted a charge sheet to the court on July 4, 2007, naming Rezaul Islam as the sole accused.
On March 4, 2008, the court framed charges against Rezaul and ordered the trial to begin.
During the trial, the court recorded testimony from 12 witnesses, including the complainant, the doctor who conducted the autopsy, the magistrate who recorded the accused’s confessional statement, the investigating officer and local eyewitnesses.
After reviewing the evidence and testimony, the court found the charges against Rezaul proved beyond reasonable doubt and sentenced him to death.
Rezaul has been absconding after obtaining bail and failing to appear before the court. The court directed the relevant police superintendent to take necessary measures to arrest him and enforce the sentence.

item.title: Home minister: Ex-Cantonment thana OC had links with AL
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said links have been found between former Cantonment Police Station officer-in-charge (OC) Md Rakibul Hasan and Awami League (now facing ban on its activities).
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the Secretariat over recent transfers of OCs at different police stations in Dhaka and the withdrawal of the OC of Shah Ali Police Station.
Asked whether merely transferring police officers could resolve problems, the home minister said transfers are an administrative measure and may be made for negligence of duty or when an officer is found to have links to certain activities.
“But the transfer is not the last step. Departmental proceedings are being taken against them after the transfers,” he said.
Referring to Rakibul Hasan, he said an investigation was conducted into the former Cantonment OC over an incident involving an audio recording that went viral on social media. He said forensic examination was also conducted and that one or two agencies were involved in the investigation.
“A case has been filed against him and departmental proceedings are underway,” Salahuddin said.
He further said charges have also been brought against Rakibul Hasan in connection with a criminal offence, including sedition, and that he has been arrested.
Rakibul Hasan came under scrutiny after an audio recording allegedly featuring his voice spread on social media.
In the recording, he was heard discussing the current situation in the police force, the posting of officers and various internal issues.
He alleged that many senior police officials are becoming involved in BNP politics while grassroots police personnel are not doing so.
He also alleged financial transactions in the appointment of OCs and the use of influential people to secure postings, while claiming that unqualified officers are being given important positions at the expense of competent officials.
In the recording, he also said the police would not be able to prevent ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina from returning to Bangladesh and expressed dissatisfaction over postings and leadership within the force.
Following an investigation into the audio, Rakibul Hasan was withdrawn from his post and a sedition case was later filed against him.
On Thursday, he was shown arrested in the case and produced before a court, which, after a hearing, granted five days' remand.
The investigation was later transferred to the Detective Branch (DB) .

item.title: BB warns against 22 unauthorized online payment platforms
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank on Sunday issued a public warning notice identifying 22 unlicensed online payment platforms operating in the country and urging the public to refrain from using or participating in their activities.
According to the central bank's Payment Systems Supervision Department, providing payment services or operating a payment system without a valid license from Bangladesh Bank violates Section 4(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, and is punishable under Section 37(1) of the same act.
The department identified the following 22 platforms providing payment aggregator services without statutory approval: BohudurPay, ZiniPay, PayTiller, BengaliPay, Payora BD, SohojPay BD, EasyPayWay, AK Pay, BD PAY, ShajgarPay, AsthaPay/CPay, UddoktaPay, Walletmix, BttPay, Easy Pay Automation, UniquePay BD, BD AUTO PAY, RH Pay BD, EzePay, AutoPay Ltd, Biswasto, and PipraPay.
The central bank advised all individuals, institutions, and businesses to refrain from conducting transactions with or engaging in the operations of these unlicensed payment aggregators to avoid legal penalties and financial risks.
Regulatory actions leading up to this notice have targeted unauthorized digital apps and platforms involved in high-interest online micro-lending, illegal gambling, and financial fraud.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and Bangladesh Bank routinely instruct commercial banks and mobile financial services (MFS) to suspend transaction channels for unauthorized platforms that bypass central bank supervision, endanger consumer data, or engage in predatory lending practices.
In July 2024, the Parliament passed the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, significantly strengthening Bangladesh Bank's statutory authority to oversee non-bank digital financial services.
Under Section 4(2) and Section 15(2) of the Act, operating any payment platform, digital wallet, or online transaction gateway without explicit authorization from Bangladesh Bank is illegal.
The law introduced strict penalties under Section 37(1), declaring unlicensed financial operations a cognizable, non-bailable offense punishable by imprisonment, steep fines, or both.
Certain platforms listed in the notice had previously faced regulatory action. For instance, Bangladesh Bank officially canceled the Payment System Operator (PSO) license of Walletmix Limited in November 2023 after detecting unauthorized and illegal financial transactions that violated regulatory terms.
Despite losing its license, platforms attempting to operate or offer payment aggregator tools without authorization remain subject to enforcement.
The Payment Systems Supervision Department launched these sweeps to mitigate systemic risks in the digital ecosystem.
Unregistered payment aggregators and gateways often lack mandatory Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) safeguards, exposing consumers and merchants to risk of financial loss, delayed settlements, data breaches, and illegal fund diversion.

item.title: NRB Bank, MetLife renew partnership for 8th consecutive year
item.description:
NRB Bank PLC has renewed its partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth consecutive year to provide enhanced insurance protection benefits for eligible credit cardholders.
Under the agreement, the bank's eligible credit cardholders will receive insurance coverage designed to help settle the outstanding balance on their credit cards in the event of death or permanent disability, subject to policy terms and conditions.
Eligible cardholders will also be entitled to an In-Hospital Cash Benefit for each hospitalization, helping them manage medical expenses during treatment and recovery.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, and Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, has signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, said: "Our customers expect banking services that add meaningful value to their everyday lives. Our partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth year will allow eligible credit cardholders to continue benefiting from insurance protection designed to support them and their families during difficult and unexpected situations."
Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, said: "Financial protection can make an important difference during an unexpected health crisis or other unforeseen event. By continuing our partnership with NRB Bank PLC, we aim to provide impactful insurance benefits that can help reduce financial worries and support greater peace of mind."
NRB Bank is one of the leading providers of card issuance and digital financial services in Bangladesh.
The bank serves customers through multiple channels, including digital banking, branch banking, agent banking, and internet banking, and offers a diversified range of modern, technology-driven banking products and services to meet customers' evolving needs.
MetLife Bangladesh, which has been operating in the country since 1952, currently serves more than one million individual customers and over 900 corporate clients.
The company continues to maintain its leadership position among life insurers in Bangladesh in claims settlement, paying Tk2,853 crore in claims in 2025 and Tk1,384 crore during the first six months of 2026, the highest claims payouts in the industry for the respective periods.
MetLife Bangladesh also maintained a claims settlement ratio of 98% in 2025, one of the highest in the industry.
Senior officials from NRB Bank PLC and MetLife Bangladesh attended the signing ceremony.
