item.title: Riaz Hamidullah: Dhaka-Delhi ties 'organic', conversation must continue
item.description:
Outgoing Bangladesh High Commissioner to India M Riaz Hamidullah has described the relationship between Bangladesh and India as “organic” and rooted in mutual interdependence and shared interests.
“Very simple - this is a relationship which, on several occasions, I've said is organic ... of mutual interdependence. It's a relationship which is in shared interests,” he said.
Hamidullah, who assumed charge as Bangladesh High Commissioner to India on April 7, 2025, is set to leave New Delhi early next month to take up his new assignment as Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations in Geneva, a senior official said.
The diplomat said differences in views, perspectives and approaches are natural in any close relationship particularly between two countries that share an intimate geography.
“But with those, we must remain engaged; carry on conversation, as we need to unpack the interaction between people far more than it is today,” he told Indian media ANI in an interview.
He said people-to-people engagement should go beyond conventional exchanges, noting that broader interaction could reach millions of people and help strengthen understanding between the two countries.
“That’s an unattended space that remains,” he said, referring to the need for greater engagement at the people-to-people level.
While communication between ministries and governments remains important, Hamidullah said he sees a much larger space that can be addressed through broader social and educational engagement.
“For example, among students, school-going children and universities,” the envoy said, adding that greater engagement in these areas could reach “millions” of people and make a “distinct difference” to the relationship between the two countries.
Reflecting on his recent experiences in India, Hamidullah, in a post on his verified X account, spoke about a visit during which an interaction with students at Delhi Public School (DPS) Srinagar left a lasting impression on him.
He visited the school after arriving in Srinagar on September 3, saying he was particularly struck by its inclusive and scholastic environment and the energy of its more than 5,000 students.
DPS Srinagar was founded in 2003 by Vijay K Dhar under the D P Dhar Memorial Trust. The Dhar family has longstanding links with Bangladesh, including through the late D P Dhar, who played a significant role in the formation and early years of Bangladesh.
Hamidullah said his interaction with students at the school offered him a different perspective on how young people view issues such as borders and identity.
A Class XII student, RJ Fatima, introduced herself to him as a radio jockey and invited him to the school's digital radio station, which, he said, has been operating since 2019.
“She just asked me and got me into her radio studio, and we got into conversation,” Hamidullah recalled. What surprised him most, he said, was Fatima’s question: “How do you look at borders?”
“Imagine, sitting in Srinagar, a girl asking this,” he said, adding that he took the question in “absolute candour” and responded to her openly.
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi recently called for keeping trade, cultural exchanges and people-to-people connectivity between Bangladesh and India moving forward, saying such issues should not be held back by political developments.
Talking to reporters after a cultural program in Dhaka earlier this month, he said the two countries would continue discussing various issues, but matters such as the Maitree Express, the Ganges Water Treaty, trade and cultural exchanges should not be allowed to get stuck.
“These are the things of ordinary people,” said the High Commissioner, highlighting the importance of keeping people at the center.
The High Commissioner said trade restrictions on both sides have to be eased. Otherwise, he noted, people will suffer.
He said there is no need to rush and the political process will take its own course. But the work that concerns ordinary people must continue, Trivedi said.
India on Tuesday reiterated that it wants to take its relationship with Bangladesh forward in a positive, constructive and forward-looking manner and expressed its willingness to discuss all bilateral issues between the two countries.
“India desires a positive, constructive, and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh,” Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said while responding to a question about bilateral ties during a media briefing in New Delhi.
Jaiswal said India is ready to discuss all bilateral issues with Bangladesh through the existing structured mechanisms.
“Our intent is to take this relationship forward in a positive direction, in a constructive direction, in a forward-looking manner,” he said.
A vibrant ‘Ilish Fest’ celebrating Bangladesh’s national fish, Ilish, was held at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi on Saturday.
The event, held at the “Maitri” Auditorium of the High Commission, brought together prominent Indian politicians, diplomats, civil society representatives, academics, journalists and cultural personalities.
During the festival, prominent Indian personalities unveiled the book A Fish Called Ilish, published in Dhaka.
The event centred on Ilish, which is deeply rooted in Bengali heritage, culture and culinary traditions. It also provided an opportunity to showcase Bangladesh’s rich cultural heritage and hospitality, with guests enjoying a variety of Ilish dishes alongside traditional Bangladeshi cuisine.
The guests appreciated not only the distinct taste of Bangladeshi Ilish but also the emotions, traditions and cultural values associated with the fish.
Former Indian Minister of State for External Affairs and noted journalist M J Akbar, former diplomat and politician Mani Shankar Aiyar, human rights activist and social thinker Syeda Hameed, former Indian ambassador Ronen Sen, eminent sociologist Ashis Nandy and other distinguished personalities attended the program.
The guests praised the taste of Bangladeshi Ilish and the overall organization of the festival.
The event also highlighted Bangladesh’s heritage, culture and hospitality, while guests expressed hope that such initiatives would contribute to further strengthening the friendly ties between the peoples of Bangladesh and India.
Speaking after the book launch, Bangladesh High Commissioner Riaz Hamidullah said Ilish is closely linked to Bangladesh’s identity and the fish is deeply intertwined with the country’s social and economic fabric.
The High Commissioner also noted that Bangladesh has five Ilish sanctuaries and that the government has taken various initiatives to increase Ilish breeding and production. These efforts have contributed to increased conservation and production of Ilish, he said.

item.title: BB governor: Int’l agreements being signed to identify, freeze laundered assets
item.description:
Initiatives have been taken to amend the "Distressed Asset Management Act" and the "Money Loan Court Act" to allow for judicial settlement within six months in order to curb defaulted loans and money laundering, announced Bangladesh Bank governor Md Mostaqur Rahman.
He stated that agreements are being made at the international level to identify and freeze assets laundered out of the country.
Additionally, 11 special joint investigation teams have been formed on the initiative of Bangladesh Bank.
He made these remarks as the chief guest at an exchange-of-views meeting titled "Implementation of Incentive Packages Announced by Bangladesh Bank for Private Sector Development" held at Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU) on Saturday (September 26).
The event was organized at the university's Syed Nazrul Islam Conference Hall under the initiative of Bangladesh Bank to raise public awareness and inform stakeholders about the package.
Regarding the recovery of the country's fragile economy, Mostaqur Rahman noted that except for foreign exchange reserves, almost all economic indicators were in a risky and negative state when he assumed office.
Multiple special plans have been undertaken for economic recovery and bringing back laundered money. At the same time, effective measures are being taken to address irregularities and looting in the banking sector.
Regarding the distribution of low-interest funds, he stated that idle bank deposits are being utilized to provide funds at 4% interest.
These funds will be distributed to the SME and agriculture sectors at interest rates between 7% and 8%.
Furthermore, the process of launching a new fund to create young entrepreneurs is underway.
Plans include offering entrepreneurs a 50% grant and loans at interest rates of 4% to 5%.
Beneficiaries will be selected through a completely transparent process involving successful private sector entrepreneurs.
In the first session of the event, attendees were briefed on the incentive package announced by Bangladesh Bank, followed by an open Q&A session where bank officials and entrepreneurs from various levels raised their issues and inquiries.
During the meeting, organizers detailed the bank-announced incentive package, stating that this entrepreneur search program will initially be conducted across 64 upazilas from 8 divisions.
Ten individuals will be identified initially from each upazila, totaling 640. Phased over time, a total of 5,000 young entrepreneurs will be brought under this financing scheme.
Based on their needs, entrepreneurs will receive a financing package of up to maximum Tk20 lakh at a profit rate of 4% to 7%, comprising 50% bank loan and 50% grant.
Presided over by Md Arifuzzaman, executive director of Bangladesh Bank's Mymensingh region, special guests included Prof GM Mujibur Rahman, student affairs adviser of the university, and SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar, Mymensingh Divisional Commissioner.
Faculty members from various university departments, senior bank officials, and entrepreneurs from different areas of Mymensingh were also present at the event.

item.title: Tarique returns home after five-day US visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home on Sunday morning after wrapping up his five-day visit to the United States to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
“An Emirates flight carrying the Prime Minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport via Dubai around 8:21am,” PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu told UNB.
After a six-hour transit stop in Dubai, the Emirates flight departed Dubai International Airport for Dhaka at 2:15am local time, Shiplu said.
Tarique arrived in Dubai from New York at 8:23pm local time on Saturday on an Emirates flight after leaving New York on Friday night.
At John F Kennedy International Airport, Tarique and Zubaida were seen off by Bangladesh Ambassador to the United States Tareq Md Ariful Islam, Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN Irene Khan and senior officials of the UN mission and embassy.
The Prime Minister arrived in New York on September 21 to attend the UNGA and delivered his maiden address as Prime Minister at the General Debate on September 24.
During the five-day visit, he held around 30 bilateral and side meetings with heads of state and government, senior international officials and representatives of international organisations.
He held bilateral meetings with the leaders of Türkiye, Iran, Pakistan, Croatia, Haiti, Bhutan and Thailand, as well as senior officials from Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Sweden.
The meetings focused on bilateral relations, trade and investment, economic cooperation, manpower, the Rohingya crisis and regional and international issues.
The Prime Minister also met UN Secretary-General António Guterres, World Bank President Ajay Banga, UN officials and other international dignitaries.
In his UNGA address, Tarique highlighted Bangladesh’s priorities on global peace and security, climate change, sustainable development, economic cooperation and the Rohingya crisis.
He also outlined the government’s three-R strategy—Recovery, Restoration and Reconstruction—to rebuild Bangladesh.
During the visit, the Prime Minister also attended high-level events on the Rohingya crisis, sea-level rise, climate action and a just transition, and integrating midwifery into primary healthcare.
On the economic front, he attended a breakfast meeting hosted by JPMorgan Chase with Wall Street representatives, where he said Bangladesh is “open for business” and invited global investors to invest in the country.

item.title: Salman Muqtadir’s studio attacked over ‘extortion refusal’; 2 held
item.description:
Content creator and actor Salman Muktadir's studio has allegedly been attacked, extensively vandalized, and looted after he refused to pay extortion money.
Salman alleged that BNP-affiliated individuals had demanded money from him, and the attack occurred after he refused to pay. Two people have been detained in connection with the incident. Muhammad Giyas Uddin, officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, confirmed this to Dhaka Tribune on Sunday morning.
He said that upon receiving news of the attack, police went to the scene, where two people were detained. He also stated that weapons were recovered. According to those involved, the incident had earlier taken place around 10:30pm on Saturday at New Greenery Properties near ECB Chattar in the capital. An official at the studio claimed that around 150 people suddenly entered the premises at 10:30pm and began vandalizing it. He alleged that several of them were carrying machetes and firearms. Seeing the dangerous situation, the officials present at the studio fled and hid in the toilet. It is alleged that the attackers followed them there as well and, at gunpoint, took their mobile phones and wallets. Various essential equipment kept in the studio was also reportedly taken. Salman Muktadir was not in Dhaka at the time of the incident. Upon hearing the news, he flew back to Dhaka. He later went to the studio, saw the damage, and addressed the matter in a Facebook Live session. Salman said the studio contained footage from various clients' shoots along with necessary equipment and materials for various projects. Because these items were taken, the extent of the damage could be substantial, though he could not immediately specify an exact figure. In the Facebook Live, Salman said that a great deal of client footage and shooting equipment had been kept at the studio, and losing them has caused both financial loss and major work-related problems. Showing the extensive damage to his studio, Salman said: "Our studio has been destroyed."
He claimed that there are very few studios like his in the country dedicated to creative work and arts and culture, and that its destruction represents an overall loss. Alleging that BNP-affiliated people were involved in the attack, Salman said: "You BNP people who did this — this is your extortion. Why are you destroying my dream?" Despite the attack, Salman said he will not stop working. Addressing his staff, he said: "Relax, this is nothing. We'll keep working right here." Salman noted that the studio was not just a business for him — it was tied to the employment and creative work of many young people. So even though the studio was damaged in the attack, he doesn't want to stop. In his words: "I will not stop. I will continue my passion. If not from within the country, then I'll continue it from abroad."

item.title: 9 arrested over vandalism, looting at Mirpur health centre
item.description:
Nine people have been arrested in connection with the looting and demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre, a private healthcare facility in Section 1 of Mirpur, Dhaka, police said.
Two truckloads of allegedly looted goods have also been recovered from the site, according to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
DMP Deputy Commissioner of Media and Public Relations Akhtar Hossain disclosed the information in a statement on Sunday morning.
He said police were identifying and arresting those involved in the attack and looting while continuing operations to recover the stolen goods.
Efforts are also underway to arrest the remaining suspects and recover the rest of the looted items, the statement said.
According to Radda, the Radda MCH-FP Centre has provided free primary healthcare, maternity and family planning services to underprivileged women and children for 50 years in partnership with the government.
Late Thursday night, heavy machinery was allegedly used to demolish the entire facility, including one permanent building and three semi-permanent buildings.
The attackers allegedly left after putting up a signboard for “Samomona Do22 Association Limited” at the front of the property.
Radda officials said a large quantity of vaccines and office equipment was looted during the attack.
Radda Executive Director Nasrin Akhtar filed a case with Shah Ali police station over the incident. The case names local BNP leader Hanif and 200-250 others as accused.
According to the case statement, a group of people entered the premises after scaling the boundary wall, carrying hammers, sticks and homemade weapons.
They allegedly beat and tied up night guards Andrio Sarkar and Abdul Hai before using an excavator to demolish several structures, including a family planning centre and the quarters of the clinic in-charge, doctor and deputy clinic in-charge.
The complaint also alleges that furniture and equipment were vandalized, while doors and windows of the ultrasound, vaccination and laboratory rooms were smashed.
The attackers allegedly took medicines and medical supplies, an ultrasound machine, generator, computers, a printer, refrigerator, air conditioner and steel cabinets.
After allegedly threatening the night guards, the attackers put up a cooperative society banner and signboard at the site, according to the complaint.
Four people arrested on Friday in connection with the incident were sent to jail by a court on Saturday.
They are Md Sohel, 22; Md Juwel, 23; Md Jihad Hasan, 21; and Md Rabbi, 20.
They were arrested during separate operations conducted on Friday night, police said.

item.description:
The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) arrested four people and seized a range of narcotics during a raid on a DJ party at a resort in Gazipur, officials said.

Acting on a tip-off, a DNC team raided a cottage named Tuberose inside the lake area of Pubail Resort Club on Friday and recovered the narcotics, he said.
The arrested individuals are Mohammad Moniruzzaman Tanjim, 29; Tushar Ahmed Nishu, 32; Mahidul Islam Rahat, 28; and Kashfia Nishat, 25.
The seized items include 21 MDMA tablets, also known as ecstasy; 24 grams of kush ; 1 gram of cocaine; four bottles of foreign liquor; 20 grams of strawberry-dream-infused gummies; a digital video recorder; three iPhones; and an Oppo phone.
Based on information obtained during interrogation, Md Emdadul Islam Mithun said Tanjim, Nishu and Rahat organised the event and operated the resort under the banner of “Sonic Plus.”
He said various types of synthetic narcotics were allegedly supplied to young men and women attending the event.

item.title: Bangladesh, Turkiye discuss PM's participation in COP31
item.description:
Bangladesh and Turkiye have discussed the possible participation of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in COP31, to be hosted by Turkiye in Antalya.
The discussion took place when State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Friday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, according to a Foreign Ministry press release.
During the meeting, they exchanged views on the upcoming climate summit, including the prime minister's possible participation. However, the press release did not mention any decision on this.

Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

item.title: LGRD minister urges students to focus on studies for brighter future
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan on Saturday urged students to remain focused on their studies and attend classes regularly, saying proper education is essential for building a strong foundation for the future.
"You must prepare yourselves for the future through education. There is no room for negligence when it comes to studies. Students must attend classes and I urge teachers to ensure that no classes are missed," he said.
The minister made the remarks while addressing a program as the chief guest at the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) of Dhaka University (DU), stressing the need to maintain a balance between academic pursuits and other activities.
"Of course, you will engage in politics, social policy and economics, but not at the expense of your education," he said. Highlighting the importance of quality higher education, Moyeen Khan said academic excellence plays a vital role in establishing a country's strength and leadership globally.
"We often talk about the United States as the world's leading nation. Many believe it is because of its wealth or advanced fighter jets, tanks and weapons. I disagree," he said.
"In my view, the United States is a leading nation because, under any recognised standard, 70 to 80 of the world's top 100 universities are American. That academic excellence has helped elevate the country to the top," he added.
Recalling the rich academic heritage of Dhaka University, the minister urged all concerned to uphold the prestige and reputation of the country's premier institution of higher education.
"The tutorial system at Dhaka University was modelled after Oxford University. If we do not preserve the reputation of this prestigious and traditional institution -- if students wander around without studying, classes are not held, and teachers and students remain absent -- how will we move this nation forward?" he questioned.

item.description:
A police member’s mother and wife were killed after a truck hit them while they were crossing a road in Dhaka’s Purbachal 300-ft area around 10pm on Friday.
The truck fled the scene after the incident, and police are working to identify it. The deceased were Afroza Akter Shanta, 28, and the mother of police member Mehedi Hasan.
Mehedi Hasan said his mother and wife were crossing the road together when the truck hit them. They were rescued and taken to the emergency department of Kurmitola General Hospital, where doctors declared his mother dead.
Afroza, who was critically injured, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for advanced treatment. She died while undergoing treatment at around 3:30am on Saturday.
Mehedi said their home is in the Sridhara area under Kadamtoli police station in Dhaka. His father, Azizul Haque, is a sub-inspector (SI) at Dhaka City Special Branch.
Inspector Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said, quoting doctors, that another woman had died at Kurmitola General Hospital in the incident. He said Afroza Akter Shanta was later taken to DMCH, where she died while undergoing treatment, and her body was handed over to the family without an autopsy.
Sohrab Hossain, officer-in-charge of Khilkhet police station, said police went to the scene after receiving the news but found no vehicle there.
He said: “CCTV footage from the scene is being collected to identify the truck involved.”
A case filed by the police regarding the incident is currently under process.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Siddique Azad granted the application and ordered that the four be sent to jail.
The accused are Md Sohel, 22, Md Jewel, 23, Md Jihad Hasan, 21, and Md Rabbi, 20.

item.title: Commerce minister: Sylhet-Dhaka six-lane highway to be fully ready by mid-2029
item.description:
The Sylhet-Dhaka highway will be fully ready for traffic after being upgraded to six lanes by mid-2029, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Saturday.
He also announced plans to establish an artificial intelligence (AI) training centre in Sylhet to help young people develop skills for the information technology sector.
The minister made the remarks as the chief guest at the inauguration ceremony of the Metropolitan Business Association at a convention hall in Sylhet city.
He said work on upgrading the Sylhet-Dhaka highway to six lanes is progressing as part of ongoing initiatives to improve the country's communication network.
Once implemented, the project will improve connectivity between Sylhet and other parts of the country and help expand investment and trade, he said.
The minister said he had discussed establishing an AI training centre in Sylhet with the ICT minister and that a final decision would be taken after bringing the minister to Sylhet next week or the following week.
He said the initiative was aimed at equipping young people with skills in the information technology sector.
“Many young people in the country are earning through freelancing. If opportunities are created for young people in Sylhet to join this sector through training, they will be able to work with different organisations at home and abroad,” he said.
Muktadir said improving connectivity, information technology and law and order was essential to increasing investment in Sylhet.
There is no alternative to infrastructure development and creating skilled human resources for the overall development of a region, he said.
On law and order, the minister said the presence of drugs or juvenile gangs in an area negatively affects investment.
He said importance was being given to strengthening technology-based surveillance to ensure security.
The minister also announced an initiative to bring Sylhet city under advanced CCTV surveillance.
He said the cameras would be capable of facial recognition and effective surveillance at night.
Leaders and businessmen of the Metropolitan Business Association attended the program.

item.title: Narayanganj trawler capsize: Three siblings found dead in Meghna River
item.description:
Three members of a family, who sank in the Meghna river after a trawler capsized in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj district on Thursday due to inclement weather, were found dead on Saturday.
The deceased were identified as Samina, 17, Sajib, 24 and Samin, 5—three siblings who went missing at the time of the accident with their father Helal Uddin, who remains missing.
The divers from local Fire Service recovered the bodies from in front of Al Mostafa Factory in Boidderbazar area of the upazila between 2:55am and 8:10am, said Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy director of Narayanganj Fire Service.
“Search operations are underway to rescue the remaining missing person,” he said.
Mohammad Zahed Chowdhury, station master of Sonargaon Fire Service and Civil Defence Station, said the trawler sank at around 1:30pm on Thursday.
On information, the diver conducted a rescue operation around 4:50pm and continued until 3am.
The operation resumed at 7am on the following day, he said.
Underwater cameras were used in the search, while divers also conducted searches using various methods, he added.
Shah Kamal, inspector and in-charge of the Boidderbazar Naval Police Outpost, said the trawler carrying 14 passengers with two cows and a goat from Homna upazila in Cumilla district sank in the Meghna River during storm on Thursday.
All of them were returning from the wedding of Sajia Akter and Shishir in Haria area in Boidderbazar of Sonargaon upazila.
Later, a woman identified as Rashida was found dead during the trawler capsize while four people including Helal and his three children remained missing.

item.description:
A separate cyber security unit will be formed next week, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Saturday.
“If a post for an additional inspector general of police does not already exist at Police Headquarters for this purpose, we will create one,” he said.
The minister was speaking at a police medal distribution ceremony in the capital.
He said branches of the new unit would be established at metropolitan, divisional and district levels.
“Police stations and district offices will be equipped with modern cyber security tools. Large-scale forensic laboratories and other necessary support facilities will be established at the headquarters and divisional levels,” he said.
The minister said he had issued directives several weeks ago to formulate a project plan for the initiative.
“Complex cases will be referred to the central unit, while cases that can be analysed at the police station, district or divisional levels will be handled locally,” he said.
“Crimes committed in cyberspace are a characteristic of modern criminal trends. In some countries, up to 44% of crimes are cyber- or scam-related. Therefore, we must attach great importance to this issue,” he added.

item.title: Prime Bank secures €20m OeEB loan to expand MSME financing
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC has recently signed a €20 million Term Loan Agreement with OeEB, the Development Bank of Austria, to expand access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Bangladesh.
Under the agreement, the financing will be on-lent to eligible MSMEs to support their business growth, expansion, investment and working capital needs.
The facility is expected to strengthen Prime Bank’s capacity to provide tailored financing solutions to businesses that play a vital role in employment generation, entrepreneurship, and economic activity across the country.
Prime Bank’s CEO Faisal Rahman, DMD Shams Abdullah Muhaimin and OeEB’s senior investment officer Ilka Vogel were present at the signing ceremony held in Prime Bank’s head office, Dhaka.
The financing reflects the shared commitment of OeEB and Prime Bank to promoting sustainable economic development and improving access to finance for the MSME sector in Bangladesh.
As the Development Bank of Austria, OeEB supports sustainable and impactful investments in developing countries and emerging markets.
Prime Bank has a longstanding track record of supporting businesses of different sizes through a wide range of conventional and Islamic banking solutions.
The bank continues to focus on expanding responsible and inclusive access to finance for MSMEs while supporting the sustainable growth of Bangladesh’s private sector.
The new facility will further enhance Prime Bank’s ability to meet the evolving financing needs of MSMEs and contribute to sustainable private-sector development in Bangladesh.

item.title: Sheltech Ceramics opens new Experience Center at Sheltech Legacy Plaza
item.description:
Sheltech Ceramics Limited (SCL) opened its newest Experience Center on September 24 at Sheltech Legacy Plaza in Banasree, marking the brand’s third Experience Center in Dhaka.
Located on Banasree’s main road, the new space brings Sheltech Ceramics’ collection of tile products to one of the capital’s rapidly developing residential and commercial areas.
The center is designed as a place where customers can see and experience products in person, from textures and finishes to different combinations and applications.
Speaking about the inauguration, Tanvir Ahmed, managing director, Sheltech Group, said: “Every new Experience Center gives us an opportunity to be closer to our customers and to understand their changing needs. Banasree has developed into an important part of Dhaka, and we see strong potential in this area. With this center, we want to make the Sheltech Ceramics experience more accessible to customers here.”
The new Experience Center is part of Sheltech Legacy Plaza, a newly launched 17-story commercial development on Banasree’s main road.
Its location offers convenient access to Gulshan, Rampura, and Hatirjheel, while planned MRT connectivity is expected to further improve accessibility to the area.
For Sheltech Ceramics, the Banasree opening builds on an expanding network of customer-facing spaces across Dhaka.
SCL already operates Experience Centers in Tejgaon and Hatirpool, each offering customers an opportunity to explore their collections beyond the traditional showroom experience.
Rather than simply displaying products, the new Banasree center has been designed to help customers experience how different tiles and surfaces work together.
This gives homeowners, architects, designers, and project professionals a more direct way to explore options and make decisions based on the actual look and feel of the products.
With its third Dhaka Experience Center now open, Sheltech Ceramics is continuing to expand its physical presence in areas where the city’s residential and commercial landscape is evolving rapidly.

Mancini finds positives in Italy loss, accepts fans' jeers
item.description:
Roberto Mancini accepted boos from Italy fans as a normal part of the game but insisted there were positives to take from a 2-0 defeat to Belgium on his return as head coach.
The Euro 2020 winner returned to the Azzurri for a second spell this summer, three years after controversially leaving the role to take a lucrative role as Saudi Arabia manager.
Tasked with overseeing a turnaround in fortunes for the four-time world champions after a third consecutive failed World Cup qualification campaign, Mancini's side got off to a bad start Friday as they were booed off at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome after losing their UEFA Nations League opener.
Speaking at a post-match press conference, it was put to Mancini that the task of winning back the fans could be like scaling Everest.
"It will be even better in the end, when you reach the top," he said. "This is quite normal, you lose and the fans are disappointed and angry, that is part of the game."
Goals from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio either side of half-time gave the Belgians a deserved win to kick off Mark van Bommel's managerial reign in style.
Italy were outplayed in spells and had goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma to thank for keeping them in the game in the first half, but Mancini saw things to build on ahead of two games against Turkey and a trip to France during the international break.
"We can pick up from the 25 minutes of the second half when we were very aggressive, recovering all the second balls, we didn't concede anything at all," Mancini said.
"This was a positive thing for me. We have to try to lose fewer balls, which is what we did in the first half, have a little more possession, with calmness and not forcing situations when there is no space."
- 'Have to let it go' -
Asked if the memory of a World Cup play-off defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina on penalties in March is still hanging over his players, Mancini said: "It's certainly something that weighs on us a little, but we have to let it go."
"We can certainly improve things, think about the positives, not always think about what has been. We can't do anything about what has happened in the past."
Former Netherlands midfielder Van Bommel was delighted with what he saw from his players as he made his debut in international management.
"I'm 100% happy and satisfied, but I understand there's always room for improvement," he said.
"We can still improve, but we started Monday with the desire and intensity we saw today. We have been working on this system for three days; it wasn't a top performance, but the desire, intensity, and control we had in the first half were excellent. We didn't concede anything.
"In the second half, we couldn't press well, even though we were well-positioned and kept our shape. (Senne) Lammens then made an incredible save. With the substitutions, we regained control of the game, and Lukebakio's amazing goal sealed the victory."

item.title: China, US to open AI ‘communication channel’ after summit
item.description:
China and the United States agreed to set up a “communication channel” for artificial intelligence incidents, both sides said, after a Washington summit short on breakthroughs.
Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discussed matters ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the United States.
Xi’s visit to Washington was marked more by pomp than substance, but the White House said on Friday the nations agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents.
Chinese state media confirmed the AI hotline was agreed in a report about the summit’s outcomes on Saturday.
While billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, Xi took a more measured tone, noting the technology must develop under human control.
The White House also reported some deals from the visit, including China agreeing to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US in 2027 and 2028.
Additionally, the two countries agreed more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of “non-sensitive goods” in each direction and two Chinese pandas were to arrive at a US zoo.
Despite the focus on pomp and ceremony during the visit, the message from the US and Chinese sides was that the summit had nevertheless helped smooth tensions between the rival superpowers over a host of issues.
Trump said the meeting was “one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the USA.”
“We’ve made great strides, very positive for both countries,” Trump told reporters as he had tea with Xi at the White House on Friday before the archives trip.
Trump rolled out the red carpet throughout the visit, treating Xi to a state banquet full of US tech titans, plus military parades, a flyover and even a tour of his new White House helipad and ballroom.
For his part, Xi said his Washington trip had added “new substance” to his summit with Trump in Beijing in May.
The Chinese leader added that they had agreed to “strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.”
The announcement that the two leaders would continue their dialogue was perhaps the biggest deliverable for both sides.
Both leaders confirmed they would meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami in December.
While visiting the National Archives in Washington, the leaders inspected the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary this year and which set out the path for American independence from the “tyrant” British king.
Beneath the rotunda, Trump also showed Xi the US constitution, the document that set out the principles of the country’s democratic government two and a half centuries ago.
“We’re just comparing how this goes 250 years, theirs goes 6,000 years,” Trump told reporters, referring to China’s ancient roots, as he stood alongside Xi, chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, which has ruled China since 1949.
Trump confirmed during the archive visit that the two leaders had discussed the US-Israeli war in Iran, which is approaching its seven-month mark.
The Republican has faced pressure from Democrats and his own party to confront Xi over reports that Beijing has supplied Tehran with intelligence for attacks on US troops.
“We did, we did,” Trump said at the National Archives when asked if they had talked about Iran.
Asked if he thought there would be progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which is crucial for the flow of oil, Trump replied: “I think we’re going to do great.”
Trump’s showcasing of US democracy at the National Archives comes a week after he banned three major US media outlets from the White House. They were readmitted on Thursday on the orders of a US judge.
The First Amendment of the US Constitution protects the freedom of the press.
Rights groups criticize China for its lack of press freedoms and the right of free expression.
Trump also publicly mocked his democratically elected predecessor Joe Biden as he gave Xi a tour of the White House on Thursday, showing him a picture of an “autopen” that he has mounted in a gallery of US presidents instead of Biden’s portrait.

item.title: Saudi coalition says intercepted Houthi drones headed for Riyadh
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles, as the Iran-backed group launched fresh attacks, including on Riyadh, despite international condemnation.
The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.
The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded “civilians, including women and children.”
The Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers, seizing swathes of Yemen’s Red Sea coast vital for oil exports and causing energy prices to jump, while also raining missiles on the kingdom.
A spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday its air defenses “intercepted and destroyed two drones launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards the Riyadh area.”
Saudi air defenses also intercepted and destroyed two Houthi-launched ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait, a city in the country’s southwest that is home to an air base, the spokesman said.
Hezam Al-Assad, a member of the Houthi Political Bureau, said on Saturday that “Despite the operation’s strength, scope, and impact, our armed forces view it as merely a small-scale rehearsal for a full-scale escalation.”
Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary general of the Gulf Cooperation Council, denounced the Houthi attacks on Saturday.
“This dangerous escalation constitutes a flagrant violation of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and poses a direct threat to the security and safety of civilians and the stability of the region,” he said in a statement.
Albudaiwi also called on the international community to “adopt a firm stance” to end the attacks and hold the Houthis accountable.
On Friday, the head of Yemen’s governing body, Rashad al-Alimi, called for a general mobilization to counter the Houthi offensive.
A ground campaign being waged by Houthi forces against Yemeni forces is threatening a humanitarian crisis, with 138,000 people displaced across Yemen since August, 70,000 children among them, according to the United Nations.

item.title: Iran proposes Hormuz plan, Trump reportedly refuses
item.description:
The United States had yet to publicly respond on Saturday after Iran offered a plan to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz, though reports indicated that President Donald Trump had rejected the proposal.
The waterway key to the world’s oil supply is central to the conflict between the US and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months, though new mediation efforts took place this week.
Iranian state media reported on Saturday that President Masoud Pezeshkian was on his way back to Tehran after attending the UN General Assembly in New York.
There he met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to the presidency, and said: “Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table, but given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States.”
Earlier in the week, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held talks with Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital shipping channel.
“Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days,” Araghchi said at the UN.
“The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure.
However, within hours of his comments The Wall Street Journal reported Trump had rejected the proposal, citing US officials familiar with the matter.
The report noted that the 80-year-old president was sceptical that Tehran would meet his demands and added he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely.
Trump also posted an image to his Truth Social platform of a map showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled “Trump Strait.”
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: “We will not cease punishing the US until Iran’s seven conditions are met.”
Iran’s plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East for seven days, including in Lebanon, according to Araghchi.
He said the conditions were the same as those laid out in a memorandum of understanding signed with the US earlier this year.
It notably calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets estimated to be worth at least $12 billion, as well as the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade of Iran.
On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz.
Pezeshkian said in an interview with broadcaster CBS that the “process will begin from the very day they accept it.”
“We had previously reached an agreement based on the MOU that was signed in Pakistan... if the United States agrees to proceed in that way, everything will return to the way it was before,” he added.
Mohebi told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands.
Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, reopen the strait and launch talks on Iran’s nuclear program.
But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.
Iran requires ships to obtain authorization before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.
Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

Sutrapur fire: Another victim dies at Burn Institute
item.description:
A 17-year-old girl, who suffered burn injuries in a fire following a family dispute at Shyambazar Chamartuli in the capital’s Sutrapur area on September 19, died at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery on Friday, raising the death toll from the incident to three.
The deceased was identified as Tania Akter.
Tania, who suffered 60% burn injuries, died at the intensive care unit (ICU) of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery around 6:45pm, said Dr Sultan Mahmud, a resident medical officer at the institute.
On September 19, five members of a family, including Mohammad Emon, a Bangladeshi expatriate in Saudi Arabia, suffered burn injuries after he set himself on fire by pouring petrol over his body following a family feud at around 4:30pm in Shyambazar Chamartuli of Sutrapur.
Emon breathed his last at the ICU of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery around 11:50am on September 20.
Four other victims — Siddique Bepari, 60, his nephew Rajib, 38, a mechanic at National Hospital; nephew Arifur Rahman Dhalu, 35, an electrician; and niece Tania Akter, 17, an honours student at a women’s college in Old Dhaka — were undergoing treatment at the burn institute.
Later, Siddique died at the same hospital on Thursday.
Among them, Emon suffered 90% burn injuries, while Siddique suffered 35% burn injuries.
All the victims live in adjacent houses on their ancestral property in the area.
Sonia Akter, wife of another victim, Arifur Rahman Dhalu, said an argument broke out between Emon’s sister Sultana and Tania on Friday over stagnant dirty water in front of their houses.
Tania asked Sultana to clean the water, following which Sultana informed her brother Emon, who returned home after learning about the dispute, Sonia said.
Emon threatened to kill everyone and himself before pouring petrol inside his room. Later, he set himself on fire, leaving all five people injured.

Bangladesh beat Indonesia for second straight Asian Games hockey win
item.description:
Bangladesh secured their second consecutive victory in the Asian Games 2026 hockey competition after defeating Indonesia 3-1 in their Pool A match at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Japan on Saturday.
Bangladesh took the lead through Amirul Islam’s penalty corner in the 11th minute.
Amirul struck again from another penalty corner in the 31st minute to double Bangladesh’s lead, before Russell Mahmud Jimmy scored a fine field goal six minutes later.
Aulia Ardh pulled one back for Indonesia from a penalty stroke in the 48th minute, but Bangladesh held on to secure all three points.
Bangladesh had earlier thrashed Sri Lanka 5-1 in their previous match after suffering defeats to South Korea (5-0) and hosts Japan (6-1) in their opening two games.
Bangladesh will face India in their final Pool A match on Monday, with the result crucial to their hopes of progressing to the next stage.

item.title: Mbappe scores but suffers knee injury as Zidane wins on France debut
item.description:
Zinedine Zidane's debut as France coach was overshadowed by an injury to captain Kylian Mbappe in a 1-0 win away to Turkey on Friday, while Roberto Mancini's first game back in charge of Italy ended in a 2-0 defeat to Belgium.
Zidane, the France legend and member of the team that won the World Cup in 1998, was taking charge of Les Bleus for the first time since being appointed in late July as the successor to Didier Deschamps.
Mbappe gave his side the lead nine minutes into the second half in the UEFA Nations League Group A1 clash at the Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, just over 100 kilometres outside Istanbul.
But the Real Madrid superstar injured himself in the process of shooting, and looked to be in clear pain when he came off a few minutes later after initially attempting to carry on.
"It's not great. Unfortunately I think he's going to have to go home. We don't want to take any risks," Zidane told broadcaster TF1, suggesting that France's all-time record goal-scorer will play no part in the three Nations League matches still to come over the next 10 days.
"He overextended his knee while shooting. It's not very encouraging."
France held on for the win without their captain, while Turkey finished the game with 10 men after goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir was sent off late on for handling the ball outside his box as he raced out to deny Bradley Barcola.
So it looks set to be without Mbappe that France will head to Brussels for their next game against Belgium on Monday.
Belgium, playing their first match since losing to eventual winners Spain in the World Cup quarter-finals, spoiled Mancini's return to the Italian national team by beating their hosts at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome.
Mika Godts of Paris Saint-Germain ran through to give Belgium a 20th-minute lead, and substitute Dodi Lukebakio fired in from outside the box to double their advantage after the break.
- Isak, Gyokeres strike for Sweden -
"We need to think positively and not keep banging on all the time about what has happened in the past," Mancini said later when asked if Italy's failure to qualify for the World Cup was still hanging over the nation.
"In any case we can't change what happened now," added Mancini, who also said that boos by the home fans in the crowd of almost 50,000 were "normal" and "part of the game".
Mancini was previously Italy coach between 2018 and 2023 and led them to victory at Euro 2020.
Elsewhere on Friday, Shea Charles of Fulham scored the winner deep in stoppage time as Northern Ireland won 1-0 away to Georgia in Group B2.
That was after PSG star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had a penalty saved for the home side.
Danylo Sikan's goal gave Ukraine a 1-0 victory in Hungary in the same group, with the visitors holding on after having Oleksandr Nazarenko sent off late on.
Robert Lewandowski captained Poland in their 0-0 draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina in Group B4, while Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres both scored as Sweden beat Romania 2-1 in Stockholm in the same section.
There were also wins for Armenia and Montenegro in League C.
The Nations League action continues on Saturday with England hosting Spain, who are playing their first game since winning the World Cup in July.

item.title: CHT minister: Concerted efforts needed to curb drugs, border crimes
item.description:
Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs Minister Sa Ching Prue has stressed coordinated efforts by the media and law enforcement agencies to address drug trafficking, border crimes and challenges related to refugees.
“Cox’s Bazar and the Chittagong Hill Tracts share close geographical and social ties. We are committed to developing Cox’s Bazar into a modern tourism city through a well-planned master plan,” the minister said.
He made the remarks while speaking at a view-exchange meeting with journalists at the Cox’s Bazar Press Club on Friday.
He said the government would work to expand tourism in Cox’s Bazar, Bandarban and other parts of the country and promote the sector at home and abroad. Expressing concern over drug trafficking, Sa Ching Prue said drugs entering the country through roads and waterways were spreading across society.
He called for drug-prevention committees in every neighbourhood in line with the Home Minister’s call. Regarding the Rohingya crisis and border crimes, he said some Rohingyas were becoming involved in drug trafficking, smuggling, human trafficking and illegal arms trading.
He proposed jointly formulating specific recommendations with the Home Ministry, law enforcement agencies and journalists and presenting them to the prime minister to address the crisis. The minister said Cox’s Bazar could be transformed into a world-class tourism city by utilizing its sea beach and the natural diversity of the hill region.
Praising journalists as the “conscience of society,” he urged them to present objective news and pledged to work for socioeconomic development.
Cox’s Bazar Press Club President Mahbubur Rahman chaired the meeting. Senior local journalists also attended.

Bangladesh calls for equitable use of shared waters, water security
item.description:
Bangladesh has called for equitable and reasonable use of shared water resources and urged international partners to turn water security commitments into concrete, measurable action.
Dr Saimum Parvez, special assistant to the prime minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change Affairs, made the call at a high-level event titled "United for Water: A Call for Collective Action" at UN headquarters in New York on Friday.
Permanent Mission of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia organized the event on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly to focus on water security, climate change and cooperation in managing shared water resources.
“Water connects us. It sustains people, economies and ecosystems. It crosses borders and underpins shared prosperity,” Dr Parvez said in his opening remarks.
He noted that climate change, rising demand and mounting pressure on freshwater are making water security increasingly difficult to achieve through national action alone.
Dr Parvez noted that shared rivers and aquifers require equitable and reasonable use, regular dialogue, timely data exchange and sound science, with mutual trust underpinning effective cooperation.
He also mentioned the importance of sustaining cooperative arrangements as climate change makes water flows increasingly unpredictable.
Calling for practical support for countries facing heightened vulnerability, he said, Climate-vulnerable countries need accessible finance, appropriate technology and capacity for resilient water infrastructure and services.”
Dr Parvez said Bangladesh, a densely populated delta and lower-riparian nation, is confronting interconnected challenges, including floods, water scarcity, river erosion, waterlogging, groundwater stress and coastal salinity.
He highlighted Bangladesh’s ongoing efforts to restore rivers, canals and drainage systems, strengthen flood management and salinity control, and expand technology-based groundwater monitoring.
He also highlighted the Government’s priority on water and environmental resilience as central pillars of national development.
On regional cooperation, he said: “Bangladesh calls for sustained dialogue among riparian countries, equitable and reasonable use of shared waters, transparent data sharing and stronger international partnerships.”
Bangladesh’s recent accession to the 1992 UN Water Convention reflects the country’s commitment to strengthening international cooperation over shared water resources, he added.
Dr Parvez reaffirmed Bangladesh’s readiness to share its experience and work with international partners to mobilize knowledge, finance and technology on water resources.

item.title: State minister: Gas supply disrupted due to delayed LNG unloading
item.description:
Gas pressure had temporarily dropped due to a delay in unloading gas from an LNG carrier amid rough weather in the Bay of Bengal, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit said on Friday.
However, the unloading process resumed at 7:18am and gas supply would return to normal by noon, he said.
The state minister made the remarks in response to questions from journalists after a district hospital health management meeting at the Jessore Circuit House on Friday afternoon.
He also said Bangladesh would benefit if fuel prices in the international market stabilise.
Speaking about ongoing health sector initiatives in Jessore, Amit said residents would receive services from a full-fledged coronary care unit (CCU) within the stipulated timeframe.
“The government is working to ensure that critically ill heart patients no longer have to travel to other districts for treatment,” he said.
He said the meeting reviewed progress in implementing decisions taken at an earlier meeting to improve healthcare services at the 250-bed Jessore General Hospital.
“Most of the decisions have made good progress, while deadlines have been set for the remaining work. Within the next few months, we will ensure that people in remote areas have access to improved healthcare services,” he said.

item.title: Cox’s Bazar airport new terminal set to open next week
item.description:
The newly built terminal at Cox’s Bazar airport will open for domestic passenger operations next week, ahead of planned international operations in October, marking a major step towards turning the tourism gateway into an international airport.
“From next week, the new terminal will be used for both arrivals and departures of domestic passengers,” Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) Chairman Air Vice Marshal Md Mostafa Mahmood Siddiq said.
The CAAB chairman, who made a final preparatory visit to Cox’s Bazar on Wednesday, said all domestic airlines operating at the airport had made the necessary preparations to shift their passenger-handling activities to the new terminal.
Airlines will initially use golf carts to transport passengers between aircraft and the terminal building, he added.
“After starting domestic operations, we will inaugurate international operations next month from this airport,” Siddiq said.
Director of Marketing and Sales at NOVOAIR Sohail Majid said the airline had completed all preparations and successfully conducted a test run to operate from the new terminal for its passengers.
“We have made all the necessary preparations, including deploying golf carts to use the new terminal,” he said.
The government is preparing to formally inaugurate Cox’s Bazar as an international airport in October following massive investment in upgrading the facility, including the construction of the new terminal and extension of the runway into the Bay of Bengal.
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat earlier expressed optimism that Biman Bangladesh Airlines, as well as foreign carriers, would eventually operate international flights from the beach city.
CAAB Member (Operations and Planning) Air Commodore Abu Sayeed Mehboob Khan said, the terminal arrangement would switch to a hybrid system once international operations begin.
Under the planned arrangement, both arriving and departing international passengers will use the new terminal.
Domestic arriving passengers will then use the existing terminal, while departing domestic passengers will complete check-in formalities at the new terminal before proceeding to the old terminal to wait for boarding.
The new terminal forms part of a broader program being implemented by CAAB under the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism to upgrade Cox’s Bazar airport to international standards and make it capable of handling wide-body aircraft.
Currently one of Bangladesh’s busiest domestic airports, Cox’s Bazar handles an average of 28 to 30 passenger aircraft take-offs and landings daily.
CAAB has implemented two development projects and one technical project at the airport to expand its capacity and facilitate direct connectivity between the country’s premier tourism destination and international markets.
The international passenger terminal, covering around 17,956 square meters, has been constructed under a project with an approved cost of approximately Tk 362.63 crore.
The terminal includes a departure lounge capable of accommodating 450 international passengers, a duty-free shop, boarding bridge, lifts, escalators, conveyor belts, check-in desks, departure and arrival immigration counters and an arrival lounge.
Four immigration desks have been installed for departing passengers and six for arriving passengers, while two baggage delivery belts have been provided for international arrivals.
PA and Flight Information Display Systems (FIDS), signage, CCTV and heavy hand-luggage scanning facilities have also been incorporated into the terminal.
The airport’s annual passenger handling capacity is expected to rise from around 730,000 to 1.8 million following the expansion.
A 36,300-square-metre apron capable of accommodating two wide-body aircraft and three Dash-8 aircraft, along with two taxiways, has already been completed and incorporated into airport operations.
Parking facilities for 35 VIP and 90 general vehicles, internal roads and other supporting infrastructure are also included in the project.
The airport has also received ICAO certification following verification of the standards required for international operations.
Another major component of the transformation is the extension of the runway from 9,000 feet to 10,700 feet, making it the longest runway in Bangladesh.
Around 43 hectares of land have been reclaimed from the Bay of Bengal to extend the runway by 1,700 feet.
The extended runway is designed to accommodate fully loaded wide-body aircraft, including Boeing 777-300ER and Boeing 747-400 aircraft.
The runway extension project has an approved cost of Tk 3,709.61 crore, while the contract value is Tk 1,794.31 crore. Chinese joint venture CYWEB-CCECC JV has implemented the project.
The project also includes around 2,200 feet of precision approach lighting extending into the sea and installation of a CAT-II Airfield Ground Lighting system to facilitate safe aircraft operations.
A 1.89-kilometre protective embankment has been constructed to protect the runway from cyclones, storm surges and other natural disasters, while security fencing, patrol roads and an 8,149-metre drainage system are also part of the project.
The government expects direct international air connectivity to help attract more foreign tourists and stimulate investment in hotels, resorts and other tourism-related businesses in Cox’s Bazar.

item.title: Ahmed Azam: Govt cannot be toppled through threats
item.description:
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on Friday said the government cannot be toppled by issuing threats and warnings, as it is a government elected by the people.
“This government is the government of the people. This government is a democratic government. This government is a government elected by the people. It cannot be toppled through threats and intimidation,” he said.
The minister was speaking at a rally organized by the Jatiyatabadi Tati Dal in front of the Jatiya Press Club before a procession.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman always seeks cooperation from the opposition over the issues they raise in parliament.
“Come, let us turn parliament into the center of all politics, all development and all prosperity. Criticize us if we make mistakes; we will correct ourselves. We will build this country with you,” Ahmed Azam quoted the prime minister as saying.
“But we are noticing that whatever the opposition says in parliament, outside parliament, they are trying hard to destabilize the government and the country. This reminds us of what Sheikh Hasina said in 1991. Sheikh Hasina said, I will not allow an elected government to remain in peace even for a minute,” he said.
The minister said the current opposition might not be using those exact words, but its activities seven months into the government’s tenure, including long marches and threats to topple and remove the government and not to leave the streets, indicate that it is following Sheikh Hasina’s approach step by step.
He, however, said the people do not like it.
Ahmed Azam said people want free and fair elections every five years under a caretaker government.
“They want elections where there will be no ballot stuffing, no coercion, no threats or intimidation. People will cast their votes; there will be no voting at night. Those who are elected by the people’s votes will serve the country for the next five years,” he said.
“We did not take responsibility to rule the country. We have taken responsibility in government to serve the country,” the minister said.
He said the opposition appears to believe that the government will fall simply by issuing threats.
The minister urged the opposition to refrain from what he described as the politics of sabotage, arson and threats.
“So, I will tell you clearly, refrain from the politics of sabotage, arson and threats like before. Speak in parliament. If we make mistakes, point them out in parliament,” he said.

item.title: Harimoto hails new era as Japan dethrone China's table tennis kings
item.description:
Tomokazu Harimoto said Japan had overcome their inferiority complex after ending table tennis powerhouse China's 32-year run as Asian Games men's team champions in a nail-biting final.
China had won gold in the event at every Games since 1994 but they were dethroned by Japan after Sora Matsushima beat Wen Ruibo in the decisive match to win 3-2.
The Japan team also featured Harimoto, whose parents were both born in China and whose mother once represented the country at the world championships.
"That we beat them was proof that we had lacked confidence before," said Harimoto, whose sister Miwa plays for Japan's women's team.
"I'm happy, but looking at the actual contest, there was nothing unusual about the way we played or the outcome.
"We just managed to attain the one thing we'd been missing -- confidence."
China's team featured world number one Wang Chuqin but his team-mates Lin Shidong and Wen are respectively ranked eighth and 15th in the world.
Japan had two top-five players in number three Matsushima and number four Harimoto.
"China used to have six or seven strong players, that's why their era lasted 10 or 20 years," said Harimoto.
"Now with two of us in the world top five, Matsushima and I can win like this."
Harimoto could not bring himself to watch the final match from the team bench after beating Wang to level it at 2-2.
"I thought it was better not to go back, a bit like a superstition," said Harimoto.
"If I was on the bench, Matsushima would see me. He probably wouldn't mind, but I minded."
Wang won the opening match against Matsushima but lost 3-0 against Harimoto.
The Chinese player said: "Psychologically, I ran into problems".
"Perhaps we panicked a little in trying to be better, and rushed some shots," he said.
China got their own back in the women's team final, beating Japan 3-0.
But the men's defeat left a bitter taste in the mouths of Chinese fans, who vented their anger on social media.
"The men's team, despite enjoying the best resources and treatment, suffers from lack of continuity and a talent gap," one user wrote on Weibo.
"There is no one coming through," wrote another.

item.title: Women’s hockey team secure historic Asian Games point after thrilling draw
